In the chilling underbelly of a secluded bunker, Donald's life was snuffed out by deadly snake venom and now, it's up to the sharp and relentless Detective Winston to shake the truth out of his prime suspects, Jay and Autumn.

I was inside the local café, mulling over the case when I saw Autumn. She was a regular here, always engrossed in a murder mystery novel, which somehow comforted me in a way. Detective work made you appreciate the mundane things about life.

"Autumn," I greeted her as I approached, "how are things?" 

She took a moment, reached down into her bag, and pulled out a specific thrilling novel titled "Perfect Crime". She glanced up from the book and responded, "Oh, hello Winston. Just the usual."

I looked down at her book, the title striking a chord, "This one any good?"

Autumn got excited and spoke in vivid detail about the perfect crime plotted in the novel. Her enthusiasm around the theme of crime and the specific details almost perturbed me, but I chose to focus on the dialogue at hand.

We mentioned Donald, and how he had plans to head to the bunker. Autumn froze for a moment before returning to her normal composure. "He trusted you," I said, "would have let you in the bunker."

"The bunker? Yeah, I know the place. Donald used to talk about it," she replied, trying to sound nonchalant. But I could discern a hint of unease in her voice, the knowledge of the bunker and everything that had transpired there appeared to weigh heavy on her.

Autumn had been in a gang with Donald. Back in the day, they used to own this town, running around and kicking up dust wherever they went. Time moved on, things had changed, but the past lingered in Autumn's fear of her past crimes revealing themselves.

Donald had confided in me once that he discovered Autumn was still engaging in criminal activities. She had psychic abilities which made her an asset in their criminal past and perhaps, in her current endeavours.

The clang of the door brought me back to the café. Autumn had left, the sunshine reflected off her hair as she headed down the street, her murder mystery novel tucked securely under her arm. The people in the café moved again, life resumed while questions circled in my mind. Along with Autumn, I left the café: one looking to uphold justice, and the other, potentially, to evade it.

Winston walked down the long, subterranean corridor again, guiding his flashlight along the intricately detailed blueprints of the bunker he held in his hands - blueprints that once belonged to the experienced Jay. Once housed in the station, this giant underground maze was a known territory to Jay, of course, but to Winston, it was all foreign.

Hours later, in a makeshift interrogation center in the surface barracks, Winston eyed the familiar face of the missionary, Jay.

"I've seen the blueprints, Jay," he said simply, watching the other man's face.

"Oh, those?" Jay replied, a light airiness showing in his reply. "I spent quite a bit of time down there when I was stationed at this bunker. I could still walk through it blindfolded."

"And isolated…" Winston added, his gaze never leaving Jay's face. It was a known fact that the underground bunker locked from the inside and the only two keys existed – one with Donald and the other with Jay. It had been established earlier that Jay and Donald were the only ones inside the fortified bunker during the time of Donald's death.

Jay didn't respond immediately. He looked disinterested, detached. He finally spoke up, "I guess Donald had started to suspect, huh? He confronted me about it a few days ago."

"You've done some snake handling, haven't you?" - Winston asked.

Jay chuckled. "A rite of passage, they call it. Over there in the region with a high snake population, it’s a trial, a blessing, an exorcism.” His tone held a grim, respectful distance. 

Winston nodded, "I've heard it's common among missionaries to learn about snakebite remedies as well."

"A living antidote, in case of a bite, that's not common knowledge."- Jay answered, leaning back in his chair.

"Were you aware, Jay," Winston began, "that Donald discovered certain… irregularities?"

Jay's eyes flickered to Winston's for the first time. "Irregularities? You mean the smuggling?" He admitted.

Winston let the confession hang in the air between them.

"I was using the missions to distribute certain substances, that part is true." Jay said.

"You got trained here, in the bunker. Now you distribute substances, in religious ruse. " His tone turned pointedly menacing. 

He leaned in slightly, resting his elbows on the tabletop, "Discovery of which, Jay, would do a lot more than tarnish a reputation."

Jay remained silent, his eyes hardening and body rigid, awaiting the impending threat the detective presented. 

Winston suddenly backed off, taking his notes and exiting the room, leaving Jay alone among his thoughts.

Background files from related investigations (some may be irrelevant):

In the tranquil world of pirouettes and pliés, prima ballerina Giselle is found dead with a syringe at a dance studio and it’s up to the steely-eyed Detective Winston to interrogate two unlikely suspects - Fred and Imogen.

Winston stared at the dance floor of the studio, reflecting on the horrific incident. Giselle, who had been practicing late in the night, was found in this one spot, a syringe sticking out. The studio was eerily quiet.

The security guard for the night, Fred, was now on the detective's radar. Guarding the studio, running its lost and found, working around the property, Fred had a significant hold on the location. Among his responsibilities was to ensure the items on the premises were secure. Recently, a syringe was reported misplaced and entered into the lost and found - the very syringe that, as per the Coroner's report, had been used in Giselle's murder.

Fred seemed more nervous than an employee should be given the circumstances. Scheduled to check properties during the time Giselle was practicing, he would have had the opportunity to interact with her. 

"Giselle...she was a hell of a dancer," Fred said, stepping away to look the dance floor. "Here late most nights, always the last to leave."

He hesitated before continuing, "She...she threatened to go to the authorities, about...about some things."

Fred's discomfort with the subject was evident. Giselle had found out about a few security lapses in the studio, and Fred was aware she had the evidence. She had threatened to report him, to show up his glaring disregard for the job he was responsible for.

Reflecting on the evidence, Winston looked at Fred. He was a night guard, in charge of property management. He had access to the studio, the found syringe, knowledge of Giselle's plans. He was more connected to the case than he probably would have liked.

Glancing back at the dance floor, Fred stared long and hard at the place where Giselle's body had been found. "I hear her sometimes, you know. The tap of her dance shoes. It's like she's still here."

Winston gave him a nod, made his notes before stepping out of the dance studio, leaving Fred alone with the haunting echo of Giselle's dance.

Winston shuffled the crime scene photos into a neat stack and replaced them in their folder. The image of the dance studio – clear aside from the single syringe lying in the centre – was fresh in his mind. He traced the edges of the file with a thoughtful brow and stood, straightening his jacket. The victim's godmother was waiting for him at her current workplace - the local hospital where she works as a nurse in her effort to pay off her debts, despite having lost her nursing job at a different hospital recently.

Imogen's life hadn't exactly gone according to plan. She used to be a respected nurse at another hospital, with a stable income, but now, despite her job at a new hospital, she was still struggling with severe debt, worsened by medical expenses she could hardly afford. One day, someone noticed Imogen with a set of keys that had been laying around the hospital. They were of a decidedly peculiar design, matching those from her former hospital. According to some people’s reports, they were similar to the ones used in prisons.

His first meeting was with Imogen herself. She was a middle-aged woman with worry lines that were etched deep into her face, a contrast from her professional demeanor at the hospital. Despite her situation, her eyes held a fierce spark of determination and resilience.

"Giselle was saving up for her future, you know," Imogen began, after the pleasantries were over. "She was a tenacious dancer, no children to her name, but wealthy nonetheless."

Winston asked about her relationship with Giselle, about her financial circumstances. Imogen was upfront about her financial issues, about how she had asked Giselle for help, despite being her godmother. She didn’t hide the fact that she had recently lost her job at the other hospital. 

Imogen shared a story about an escape plan she cooked up once. It was detailed and quite intricate, considering it was made up on the spot during a party. It was said in jest over drinks, but the detail of the plan was plausible to say the least.

Winston left the woman with a curt nod, wondering if Imogen’s elaborate plan was simply the ramblings of a desperate woman or perhaps, more than that. Her life, after all, had not worked out the way anyone would have hoped. And life, he knew, had a tendency of pushing people to do things they never thought they could.

In the eerie silence of a wrestling ring, Stuart's life was brutally ended with a lead pipe, leaving Detective Winston with a chilling case and two prime suspects: Shawn and Octavia.

Winston sat on the bench outside the state penitentiary, going over the leviathan-sized stack of Octavia's prison records, flicking out the pages one by one. They depicted the daily life of a woman maintaining an intense physical regimen. She was fit, she was disciplined. A disciplined, successful wrestler.

The sun faded into the horizon as he stared at the record of the wrestling event Octavia had been part of and for which she had been granted a day-release pass. The sign-off from the warden stood out even in the dimming twilight. In Winston's years of experience, it was a rare thing for a prisoner to be given such a privilege, but to wrestle? That was unheard of.

Octavia, however, was an exception. She reportedly kept up her wrestling training in prison, rigorously keeping in shape. This explained her winning streak in the prison's wrestling records. But it didn't explain everything.

A chill wind swept through the yard and Winston flipped a page, his eyes catching on a note about Octavia's disciplinary actions. Several infractions, including her use of illegal foreign objects in wrestling matches, her attacks on other inmates – even using a tray as a weapon once – were duly noted.

It was the mention of her being caught as she attempted to steal from the prison’s medical ward though, that drew Winston's attention back. This was a woman fighting, desperate even, against the grips of drug addiction. Withdrawal symptoms were known to be brutal, but rarely did prisoners resort to such extreme measures.

Moving next to Stuart's file, it was clear his troubles began long before his death. Notorious from his time smuggling drugs, he later succumbed to the law's pressure and put a stop to his operations. It was a known fact he later became a regular at wrestling events, noticing Octavia there more than once. A rehabilitation, or an escape, who could tell?

Whether his love for wrestling drew him into proximity with Octavia, or his previous life of drug-running played a part, was unclear. But while drug addiction had inflamed Octavia’s desire for the substances Stuart had dealt in his past, she too shared a passion for the wrestling spectacles for which he was known. Their paths certainly crossed more than once on wrestling's squared circle.

As Winston compiled his notes, having immersed himself in the life histories of both Stuart and Octavia, he felt a strange connection between them. The pieces were there. Now, he just had to fit them together into a telling tale of how this wrestling ring turned into a crime scene, and transformed a fit, strong woman into a suspect.

Shawn's home was an impressive sight, and the library even more so. Winston noticed it immediately upon walking in, walls nearly toppling over with books. A slight air of dust hung in the quiet, still air of the room. Some of the book spines jumped out at him - collections of works on serial killers - but he reminded himself to stay focused on his task at hand.

"Detective Winston," Shawn greeted him, rising on his entry, "Please have a seat." 

"Thank you, Shawn," Winston complied, glancing about the room. “Impressive library. Do a lot of your work in here?” 

Shawn nodded, gesturing around the room, "Yes, my sermons take a lot out of me, and preparation requires time. I often seclude myself in my study, preparing for my sermons. My faith is the core of my being, detective.” 

Winston nodded, listening to Shawn talk proudly about his devotion to his faith. He did not interrupt when Shawn spoke of his religious rituals involving lead pipes that he had been taught by elders of his faith. 

Shawn leaned back in his armchair, wiping a bead of sweat from his forehead, "In fact, detective, on the night of the incident, I was conducting a sermon for our group, right here in my home study, followed by our ritual at the wrestling field. Stuart solicited my presence to view the wrestling match and then to conduct the closing rituals."

"And how do you normally feel after these rituals? You look a bit tired, Shawn," Winston softly asked.

Shawn rubbed his eyes and sighed, "Studying and my religious work often tire me. It's a lot of late nights, yes..."

Winston nodded and stood up to leave, "I appreciate you taking the time to chat with me, Shawn. I'm sorry for your loss." 

Shawn thanked him and Winston left, noting the enclosing quiet of the study once more before he did. The library lingered in his mind, but he shut that thought away as he walked out of the house.

Target case file:

When fitness enthusiast Uma is ominously murdered with a vial of acid at her local gym, it's up to seasoned Detective Winston to unravel the mystery between the two prime suspects, Irving and Addison.

Detective Winston was indoors on another stifling California afternoon. His attention was fixed on the Irving case, a case that kept him on his toes for several days now. A screenwriter suspected in the murder of a fellow gym goer. He couldn’t help but feel the increasing pressure of the time crunch.

Irving was not an ordinary man. Winston had discovered from the interviews and police records that the guy particularly had some weird habits. Irving, it seemed, was battling insomnia and was unable to sleep in his own home at night. During these restless nights, he would busy himself with his notebooks. Often, he was seen at the fitness center, sketching intriguing symbols into his notebook, which he always carried along with his pencil. He would leave home with these immediately after sunset.

One specific detail that struck the detective was Irving's fascination with themes and symbols of the past, particularly those formed by ancient gravestones. These ancient symbols were found in notations and sketches strewn across his notebooks. It was curious to Winston how an old world art found a home in the hands of a modern screenwriter.

His insomniac late-night habits weren't the only thing that raised suspicions, though. Irving also was a member at the same fitness center Uma frequented, spotted regularly training late into the night. The very same fitness center that was the scene of the crime. The records substantiated his presence late on the night of the murder. Like the deceased Uma, he seemed to utilized the solitude that the near-empty gym provided, allowing him ample time alone.

The lines on Winston's forehead became more pronounced as he read on. He found a strange connection between both Uma's and Irving's lives. Not only did they work out at the same gym, but they also shared a professional conflict. Reports indicated that Uma had discovered Irving's success was largely built on her own work which he'd plagiarized. Fearing public humiliation and the definite demise of his screenwriting career, Irving had a lot to lose. To make matters worse for Irving, Uma, the aggrieved, had threatened to expose his deceit to the public.

The tension of the case was truly weighing on Winston. He sighed, leaning back from his desk. Questions in his mind demanded answers that weren't there yet. So, he decided to continue with the investigation, waiting for the breakthrough that would add some clarity to the clouded picture. He had a late-night meeting with the prime suspect, Irving, in the pipeline. It was indeed time to probe further and extract some answers from the silence of the night.

Detective Winston admired the modern glow of the fitness center that served as his next stop in the investigation. The thudding of footfalls on running machines, the humming of weight machines, and the faint scent of sweat and disinfectant whispered of a place that had teetered on the edge of life and death.

"Lookin' to join?" came a voice from behind him. He languidly turned to find Addison, the local trainer.

"No. Detective Winston, on official police business," he presented his badge.

The sour taste of surprise was evident on Addison's face, "We're an excellent gym with a friendly vibe; it's a shame. You don't say, a detective?"

"I've checked the fitness center security cameras," Winston watched as Addison pressed his lips together, "Noticed you were entering the gym shortly before time of Uma's death."

Addison placed a hand on a weight machine, lowering his gaze to his feet. "Uma? You mean my client, Uma? We were scheduled for a training session that day."

Winston opened his notebook, scanning his notes, "You have a background in chemistry, is that right?"

Addison looked up from his shoes, "Yeah, I even teach it at the high school. Possess a chemistry degree and recently purchased a chemistry set for demonstration."

"Interesting. The set contains vials of acid, science class protocol?" Winston asked, his brow furrowing.

"Absolutely, controlled experiments to teach risk and safety," Addison said, transported into the world of academia. The detective noticed a flicker in Addison’s expression as he continued to speak but brushed it off, it meant nothing yet.

A few people from the gym had crowded around now. They watched as Winston asked, "Can you recall Uma saying anything about the honesty of the staff or maybe about any missing equipment?"

"Well," Addison began, rubbing his neck, "Uma did once vouch for me, said I was honest and commendable, a good character, you know." He looked around the room and swallowed. "And yes, she did mention once about missing equipment. Unfortunately, she also stumbled upon some CCTV footage of me taking some expensive equipment. I had intended to return it, it was a mistake. "

As Winston watched the gym members disperse, he looked back at Addison. "So, Uma caught you stealing from the fitness center. That must've been uncomfortable for you. It surfaced in the investigation that fitness equipment has been reported missing recently. Uma seemed to have discovered the theft."

Addison suddenly seemed to find the floor tiles fascinating. "Uma was a good woman," he said quietly. "It's a shame what happened to her."

"Agreed," Winston replied, closing his notebook. "Keep a clear schedule, Addison. We'll be in touch."

As Winston exited the gym he took one more glance at Addison through the large glass panes. Cold air nipped at his face and Winston pondered the car ride back to the station.

Background files from related investigations (some may be irrelevant):

In the tranquil vineyards, Terry's life was brutally snuffed out by a makeshift shiv, and now it's up to seasoned Detective Winston to unravel the truth from suspects Bella and Jose.

Winston's gaze riveted to the roughened edges of the shiv, incapable of focusing on anything else; it was a creepy reminder of the gruesome murder witnessed by the perfectly lined vineyards.

"Terry didn't deserve this," He muttered to himself, picturing the crime scene near the shed where the body was discovered.

The intern, Bella, had been a suspect from the start. Her thread of criminal activities had caught her in quite a controversy at the vineyard. It was impossible to miss her confrontational personality - as though she was daring someone to stop her when stealing exquisite, rare, and expensive wines for her personal collection.

Winston couldn't help but contemplate the strange occurrence in Bella's personal life. Young men entered her domain and exited as quickly as they had appeared, never to be seen again. With every month, a new face would hover around Bella and by the end of the month, he would be gone, replaced by someone new. Each of Bella's ex-boyfriends had immediately relocated after their breakups, disappearing from the local scene completely. It was a peculiar pattern; the complete absence of these ex-boyfriends aroused his curiosity.

What intrigued him further was Bella's striking composure amidst the turmoil of her fluctuating relationships. As impassive as the vineyard's stoic trellises after a heavy rainfall, she remained unfazed.

Winston glanced at his notes again. She had been working in the vineyard on that fated day. Scratched and scuffed, the details of her encounter with Terry taunted him. They were seen arguing earlier in the day in the very vicinity where Terry's lifeless body was discovered later on.

Terry confronted Bella about her escalating thefts. He even threatened to report her consistent wrongdoings to the management. Winston could still hear Terry's exasperated voice echoing through his memory, "I won't ignore your actions anymore, Bella."

He knew he had to remain as neutral as possible. He had an interview with Bella later that day. Still, he was haunted by the fact that Bella was spotted close to the murder shed minutes before Terry's untimely death. The evidence seemed to be tediously compiling against her, even if he couldn’t make a judgment yet.

As he left the confines of his office, he carried with him a myriad of unanswered questions stirred by Bella's questionable activities and peculiar patterns. He couldn't share his suspicions but had to continue peeling the layers off Bella's shrouded lifestyle to find the truth about Terry's unfortunate demise.

Winston pulled up to the vineyard. Terry had been found stabbed there with a shiv, a simple tool turned deadly in wrong hands. As a detective, he had seen a variety of murder weapons, but this was unusual for the calm and serene vineyard setting. A vineyard, that was owned by the very victim, Terry. 

He could see Jose, hard at work on a new structure. Not surprising, as the police records stated that Jose was a construction worker assigned to the vineyard project.

In a staccato rhythm, Winston released a volley of questions towards Jose. "You were working here when Terry was murdered?" Jose merely nodded, the mid-day heat not offering much conversation. 

The fact that Terry was also on the vineyard premises when his murder occurred wasn't sheer coincidence. He owned this place and had the habit of visiting regularly and checking on things. Like a suspicious owner, which might have driven him to suspect theft and falsify work hours.

Winston decided to indulge in those eve`s dropping senses and questioned Jose discreetly, "I heard Terry was saying something about someone stealing tools from the site. Also, there was a rumor that Terry had found out about some false time-sheets. What do you say, Jose?" 

"Well, sir, I won't lie," Jose said, after a moment of elaborated silence, "He did accuse me of theft and false time-sheet matters. It's true, Terry had discovered I was falsifying my work hours. But, I wouldn’t dare do such things." The accusation was serious enough that Terry had even threatened to dismiss Jose. 

And with dismissal came a perilous reality for Jose - complete shortfall of income. "Call it fate Sir, but I was really worried as this was solely my source of income."

This was common knowledge among construction workers that their job gave them access to a variety of tools, possibly even those that potentially could be turned into a simple weapon like a shiv. Many of the tools that could be found on a given construction site had sharp edges and could easily be fashioned into a homemade knife.

"Winston, the construction work often involves building and crafting things from a number of materials. It's just that, it's a hands-on job. But it doesn’t mean we all are knave, sir." 

Seeing the sun dipping into its sunset, Winston thanked Jose for his time before getting back into his car. As he mused over the case he was dealing with, he realized it was anything but simple... just as dark and complex as the ripe grapes in Terry's vineyard.

In the frost-kissed tranquility of a chalet, Malaysia meets a fatal end by a rifle's sinister call, hurling Detective Winston into a tense investigation with suspects Letti and Evelyn.

Detective Winston entered the shop, the aroma of gunpowder and oil clinging to every corner. His gaze landed on Evelyn, her practiced fingers brushing over the rifles on display, particularly one that matched the murder weapon's description from the Malaysia case. He ambled over calmly, revealing his badge.

"Evelyn, mind if we chat?” He enquired.

With mild surprise playing on her face, Evelyn swiveled towards him. “Ah, Detective, how can I assist you today?”

Winston, leaning on nonchalance billowed, “Just a small query. The sales records I stumbled on here mentioned that you recently purchased a rifle quite identical to the one involved in the Malaysia case.”

Evelyn adroitly diverted, “Let’s not linger on such topics. How about a tarot reading instead? Or we could discuss hunting, I've been prowling the wilderness for decades. In fact, just the other day, I snagged a massive buck, a regular for me. Larger than any man I've encountered.”

Unfazed by the segues, Winston steered back. “Last time you took a trip to Malaysia?”

Evelyn’s countenance eased recalling her frequent visits. “Just last week, I made my usual jaunt to her chalet. Always adored that one, coveted a place just like it in the area. I suppose the keys she gave me showed her trust.”

Ignoring her indirect admission to possessing the chalet keys, Winston pointedly continued. “Evelyn, I've heard whispers about your past in corrections. Is it true that you were under investigation for a suspected misconduct? I do remember reading files that mentioned questions raised by your superiors regarding your professional ethics during your tenure at the correctional facility.”

Evelyn held her breath for a moment, eyes sparking with irritation, but deflected towards the familiar haven of her tarot readings. “Detective, ever contemplate the influence of fate? This morning, the Death card surfaced in my reading, symbolizing drastic change.”

Detective Winston didn't dwell on her diversion. He pressed on, “So, it's confirmed then? Malaysia left you her chalet after her unfortunate demise?"

"Yes,” Evelyn confirmed softly, nodding. “Yes, she did."

After a brief silence, Winston added, “One more thing, I recall seeing your name in the investigation report at your job. It outlined allegations of misconduct against you and even raised questions about your professional ethics. Is that true?”

But before he could push further, Evelyn interjected swiftly, "Who wants to ponder over the past? This tendency of mine to bring up tarot readings when questioned about my past career—it’s my distraction mechanism, Detective. The imminent future is what fascinates me." Spotting a chance, she jumped. "Speaking of which, I heard you’ve again taken up hunting, Detective?"

"Yes, I have," Winston affirmed, adeptly bypassing her attempt to wrench away the conversation.

Evelyn smiled, a small curl to her lips as her fingers lightly stroked the barrel of the recently purchased rifle, "Good, keeps the senses sharp."

Detective Winston was left to muse over Evelyn's diversions as he took his leave. His gaze involuntarily travelled to where Evelyn's fingers were tracing the rifle. Once a hunter, always a hunter—and in this round, it was hunting for answers to the Malaysia case.

Dusk was setting in as Detective Winston pulled up to the chalet. The picturesque scene was offset by the grim red crime scene tape adorning the front entrance. "Ironic," Winston muttered as he absentmindedly flicked his thumb over a fingerprint report. The details confirmed the rifle found was indeed registered under Letti's name. As he scanned the report, he noted Letti’s previous acknowledgement that the rifle was kept in her home. He climbed out of the vehicle and stepped into the biting cold.

In the chalet, a collection of hunting memorabilia and photos gathered his attention. Winston found it chill-inducing as he thumbed through photos of Letti grinning, rifle in hand, next to her game. He placed the pictures back meticulously where they belonged and proceeded to dust for prints on the rifle held up by a mounted rack, his brow furrowed in thought.

His thoughts were interrupted by a knock at the door. "Detective Winston, we have Letti on the line," a young officer said, hesitantly.

"Thanks." Winston said, grabbing the receiver, "Letti, can we talk about your activities on the night of the murder?"

"Of course, detective. I spent the entire evening at home, watching TV," was Letti’s all too casual reply. "But the night before, I stayed in the chalet, alone and hunting,” she added casually.

Outside, Winston approached Letti's car. He silently took in the snow-encrusted vehicle, its presence at the chalet the night before the murder a fact that couldn’t be unseen. 

A notification beeped on his phone - an alert about Letti’s social media activity. A quick scroll revealed a series of disturbing posts filled with racist vitriol that Letti hadn’t even bothered to hide.

Later that day, he interviewed people from Letti's neighborhood. A gentleman shared his disapproval of Letti's behavior at a recent public event: "She publicly made offensive and racist comments, unprovoked!," he spat while shaking his head. Another testimony came from Malaysia's new boyfriend who claimed that Letti had approached him with hostile intent.

In the middle of his inquiries, Winston received a distressing message from a fellow officer. It was a tip that someone had reported Letti for an act of terrorism at the chalet. The exact same chalet where tonight’s murder occurred.

Winston's mind ran back to the incident reported at the chalet. As he revisited the scene, he spotted a rifle case gathering dust, triggered by the memory of seeing Letti's registered firearm at the murder scene. 

"Don't you go shooting every weekend Letti?" Winston asked in a casual conversation.

"Yes detective, I find it therapeutic..." Letti trailed off. 

Winston concluded the day by visiting one of Letti's friends who looked nervously at her hands as she said, “Letti was unusually upset about Malaysia's new relationship. She couldn’t quite hide it…”

Winston nodded, "Alright, thanks for coming in. We'll keep in touch."

As he got back in his car, he looked up at the rapidly darkening sky. Another puzzle piece found. Now, onto the next one.

Target case file:

In the cold echo of a deserted hockey rink, Otis was found dead from a grenade explosion, and now Detective Winston must decipher the clues, suspecting Ervin and Andrew are somehow involved.

Winston let out a pensive sigh as the medical examiner rattled off the factors that spelled foul play, namely the shrapnel directly linked to a grenade. When you see something new, you remember it, he mused.

The town had been buzzing since Ervin's angry outburst in the synagogue last Sunday. Bystanders had recounted to Winston how Ervin had been shouting at a particular customer he had been consulting with, before the outburst escalated and he stormed off into the synagogue. The same customer Walter Harrison was who Ervin had consulted with before he stormed off into the synagogue, had recounted it to him with fear in his voice.

"And you say you were trembling after the confrontation, Mr. Harrison?" Winston asked after the customer finished recounting Ervin's worrying reaction.

"N-not just a confrontation," the distressed customer stammered, "Ervin, our Rabbi, he lost it – punching the walls, shouting at everyone. There’s still a visible dent where he hit."

Winston gave a slight nod, “Thank you for your cooperation,” he said before heading toward the synagogue to track down Rabbi Ervin.

Ervin Thornberg, the Rabbi, met Winston's inquiring gaze coolly. Ervin had a hardened look - the clear evidence of his military past. He was known in town as former military officer with specialized training in demolitions. Nothing could erase that part of his life.

"Quite an impressive array of memorabilia here, Rabbi," Winston remarked, scanning the room filled with various wartime relics like grenades and medals from Ervin's service days. "Your friends often tell stories of you proudly showing these off."

"Careful with those, Detective, they are from my time in the service," Ervin replied, with a hint of nostalgia creeping into his tone. "My friends, they have a way of making things sound more dramatic."

Winston was further intrigued by the hint of gossip he received from one of Ervin's neighbors, "You know, Otis had been vocal lately. He saw something he shouldn't about Ervin and the synagogue funds. Even said he was planning to go to the authorities."

With that information, Winston pitched it to Ervin, "I hear Otis saw something alarming involving you and the synagogue's funds. Heard he was seriously considering going to the authorities."

Ervin stiffened noticeably, his cool gaze flickered for a moment. "Otis talks too much," he muttered, a subtle hint of annoyance in his tone.

Just as he was about to leave, a troubling fact popped back into his mind - Otis. Otis had seen Ervin embezzling funds from the Synagogue and Ervin knew that. Winston marked it down mentally and with a brisk nod to Rabbi Ervin, made his exit. Feeling the sharp gaze of Ervin boring into his back, he needed no further confirmation.

The pieces were neatly aligning, like pieces of a puzzle, Winston could see it - But it wasn't his place to tell the story, rather gather it. So with another sigh, he slid into the driver's seat and drove off. The knot in his gut tightened as he pulled away from the synagogue - he knew his work here was far from done.

Winston pulled the collar of his jacket up and stepped into the freezing cold of the hockey rink. Alone in the rink, he squinted under the heat of the artificial light to read the deserted stands and make out the chalk lines: "Just a man and his routine...Otis was always here at this time, when no one else was present...So why Otis? Why here?"

Hours later, Winston found himself wading through the mud and foliage of a nearby hiking trail. He was there to meet Andrew, the local hiking guide, a formally trained Bomb Disposal Technician in the military, and a close friend of Otis. Andrew's hiking business had been losing traction for quite some time. His soldier-like formality was still intact, standing tall despite the fall of his flailing business, which was evident through alarming financial reports showing consistent and increasing negative balance in his accounts.

"Right this way, detective." Andrew offered, leading him through the dense woods with the authority and precision that only a man with his specialized training would possess. Andrew diligently used his army skills to ensure the safety of hikers from any potential environmental dangers on their guided tours.

"Andrew-" Winston began, striding to keep up with the trained speedwalker, "I was told you two were close. And you had asked Otis about his insurance policy recently. Care to shed some light on that?"

Andrew did not look back as he continued walking. "Sure did. Otis had been open about his routine. I always knew when he was at the rink or off somewhere else. As for his insurance, he had approached me for advice and later updated it, naming me the beneficiary."

As they neared Andrew's hiking spot, Winston noticed a military-grade tent with tools, knives, ropes, canned food supplies, and hidden among them, explosives. Andrew's intense secrecy hinted at something more - these were not just regular hiking supplies.

"Quite a collection here, Andrew. Comes in handy during your hikes I presume?" Winston asked casually. Andrew replied with a nod, "It's an efficient system. Every item serves a purpose."

Before Winston could probe further, his phone buzzed, indicating a call from the station. "Just bear with me, Andrew," Winston excused himself. Andrew shuffled uncomfortably nearby, sparked a further conversation about Otis' recent insurance update.

A forensic update from the station linked the lethal grenade to the recent military base theft!

"Do you mind if we take this conversation downtown, Andrew?" Winston turned around. Andrew stood tall, showing no signs of discomfort. He simply nodded and followed Winston, all the while maintaining his usual formal demeanor.

Background files from related investigations (some may be irrelevant):

In the glitz and glamour of a bustling casino, a deadly secret unfolds as Iris is found lifeless by a lead pipe, leaving Detective Winston with two puzzling suspects - Madison and Christine.

Winston struck a match, lighting his pipe and eyeing his case files splayed out on the desk before him. He had a slight headache after a long day of looking into the mysterious death of a lady called Iris. A sad story really, she was a frequent visitor at the casino, she had the luck of a devil. She often walked out of that place with a smile on her face and a hefty amount in her purse...until the night she didn't walk out at all.

Sifting through the evidence, Winston's hand found an envelope labeled 'Confidential.' Inside, there was a recorded statement Iris had given to a trusted friend a few days before her death. Iris clearly expressed her intention to report Christine at her next police visit.

The only real link he had to the case so far was Christine. Christine was a solid, muscular woman who worked long hours at a construction site. It wasn't just her construction job that kept her fit, it was also the time she spent with Iris working on a shared construction project. It was during these long hours they spent together that they built a strong association, a teamwork which often led them to the casino.

Christine, during one of their teamwork endeavors revealed to Iris her involvement in certain illicit activities. Iris, shocked by this revelation, clearly intended to report these activities to the police, a fact she expressed in the recorded statement Winston now held in his hands.

Another peculiar detail, a lead pipe -- the same type as the murder weapon -- was discovered at Christine and Iris's collective work site. Christine certainly had the brawn to wield that pipe.

Winston flipped open the file and spread out the still shots from the casino's surveillance footage. A timestamp in the corner corroborated with his notes -- Christine was present at the casino the night of the murder.

The police station was quiet as he entered Christine's holding cell. The woman looked tense but tried to put up a brave front.

"Spending a lot of time at the casino and the construction site these days?" He asked.

"Sure, ever since Iris and I started working on that project together. We often celebrated our small victories at the casino" Christine's voice choked a bit on her friend's name.

"And during those hours you told Iris about your...extra-curricular activities?" Winston pressed further. Christine didn't deny it, remained silent.

"Iris had planned to turn you in you know?" Winston said coolly, fanning out the recorded statement. "This was her intention during her upcoming visit to the police station."

Christine didn't respond, just locked her gaze onto Winston's.

"I noticed a lead pipe lying around your shared construction site, identical to the murder weapon," he pushed further. "Now, Christine, what else did you two discuss when you were working on those projects?"

Winston sat back, letting his words linger in the chill air of the interview room. The pieces of the puzzle were slowly falling into place, but the game was far from over.

Detective Winston scoured through the casino surveillance footage once again, his grim reflection faintly visible on the monitor screen. There was Madison, peering into what looked like a 'souvenir' box, a curious mix of nostalgia and uncertainty etched on their face. Not a lead, but perhaps another piece of the puzzle.

A separate clip caught Winston's eye, revealing Iris within the casino, merrily wagering lady luck amidst a sea of other gamblers. Iris and Madison under the same roof. It made sense something had transpired, but it was not his place yet to jump to conclusions.

Subsequent investigation took Winston to Madison's apartment. Reports had come in that they were often seen witnessing Iris's Friday night departures for the casino. Madison, it seemed, had an insight into Iris's late-night gambling endeavors, if only because they both shared the same neighborhood.

A new twist arrived in the form of an overheard conversation. Madison, just within earshot of Winston's position, seemed to be reminiscing about overhearing Iris's tales of the casino's allure. It didn't boost the investigation, but it added an interesting dynamic.

As the day wore on, Winston moved to the next building with a lead. Madison, seen using a key to enter the previous tenant's apartment, raised some questions. On being questioned about possessing this particular key, Madison nostalgically said, "Ah, such memories." The janitor confirmed that Madison had indeed requested a copy of the previous occupant's keys. A favor for an old friend or something more sinister?

The detective moved his inquiry to the legal hullabaloo that suddenly had Iris at the heart of it. Surveillance footage showed her in the courthouse with an armful of court documents. Iris was no ordinary casino patron but a key witness in a court case directly linked to Madison's illegal activities. This implied a new layer of complication to their association.

Legal terms printed on an eviction notice in Madison's possession stated that any illegal activities could lead to immediate eviction. Madison, having received this, was acutely aware of the implications of Iris' testimony.  A visit to the casino and the courthouse, another twist in the tale, was when Madison's lawyer had to break the news to their client about Iris's damning testimony.

But for Winston, there was still a bunch of questions left unanswered, and the jigsaw was only half complete. The investigation had to dig deeper. There was a long day ahead. Pieces were moving, and Winston knew well enough in this game; nothing moved without a reason.

In the seemingly peaceful city zoo, Stuart's life was brutally ended with a hatchet, and now it's up to Detective Winston to uncover the truth among suspects Xanthe and Lowell.

As Winston left the precinct, his mind was in a swirlwind. Investigating the murder of Stuart gave him a bone-chilling sensation. The images of the crime scene fresh in his mind. But a crime scene found in a zoo? He needed answers.

Entering the coffee shop where Xanthe worked as a barista, Winston could see several customers waiting in line. Apparently, their coffee was popular in town. Xanthe could be seen behind the bar, engaging her clients, before she gracefully hurried over to the espresso machine. In that hurry, she accidentally drops a piece of paper. A customer quickly pointed it out, and Winston intervened to pick it up. 

"That looks like a list of phone numbers," the customer said, peering over Winston's shoulder and noticing the peculiar numbers. "Those aren't usual business or personal contacts. I work in telecommunications, I know."

"Thank you," Xanthe said, acknowledging the mishap, before busying herself again. 

Winston headed to the bar but opted not to order anything. Instead, he scanned the fallen paper. The now identified phone numbers seemed quite out of place.  

The Zoo's visitor logs showed that Stuart was a regular, showing up daily. He made a mental note of that. There was certainly a connection between Stuart and the coffee shop...with the baristas. Stuart was seen being quite friendly with the baristas, including the newcomer, Mary, whom he praised quite often. 

"Was Stuart a regular here?" Winston asked Xanthe.

"Yes," She responded warmly, "he loved our coffee. Always praised Mary's hand.. She's pretty good, new or not. But you know, I was the one who used to make his coffee. Had his special recipe down, I did," She added, pointing towards a different espresso machine designated for complicated orders.

"Oh, that's interesting. You must have a busy schedule," Winston said offhandedly.

"Oh yeah, it includes working weekends too," Xanthe said, giving off a slight chuckle.

As Winston left the coffee shop, he recalled that Stuart's murder happened on a weekend. Winston knew this wasn't a coincidence, there was a complex web of intrigue developing here, leading him deeper into the mystery.

Winston stared at the emails on Stuart's computer screen, reading about the deep financial holes Lowell had dug for his bank’s high profile clients. The source of these emails was unidentified, but they were enough to start a full-scale fraud investigation. It appeared that the businessman had been trading emails with Stuart not too long ago. It wasn't too hard to figure out why Stuart might've been targeted.

He looked over the police report, his cigar glowing in the dim room. It was late afternoon when the banking industry slows its hustle and bustle, that Stuart was found at the zoo. It was also the same time Lowell had a bank meeting at the branch near the zoo, according to the calendar reminder from Lowell's heavily incriminating laptop.

As Winston took a break from the case files, sipped coffee, and thought about his next move, he knew he needed to get over to the lumber yard. The police had found some rather interesting pieces of evidence there. The man behind the desk at Lowell's bank vouched that he was a regular at the nearby lumber yard and had been for years. With an empty shed filled with sawdust and shards of wood at his home, it made sense where most of the firewood at Lowell's house came from.

Shuffling through the paperwork, Winston found a bank withdrawal receipt from Lowell's office. It was the bank near the zoo. The timing was convenient. As were the missing firewood logs from his backyard. The man certainly had spent a lot of time around there, in the late afternoon.

The next stop for Winston would be the café. Sure enough, the receipts and CCTV footage confirmed that Lowell was a regular there as well and was there around the same time Stuart was at the zoo.

The guy at the lumber yard confirmed that Lowell came in pretty frequently, mostly for firewood and sometimes for tools. Most recently, he had come in for a new hatchet, but he mentioned that his old hatchet was missing from his shed. Strange, considering the murder weapon was a hatchet and it just so happened to match the brand that Lowell usually favored.

In his search, Winston found Lowell's laptop at Stuart's apartment. Through Lowell's email exchanges and Stuart's search history, it became clear that Stuart had found evidence of Lowell's illegal banking operations. These were the same operations he had been contacting the unknown source about. And there were the emails from Stuart himself, asking for a substantial dollar figure to keep quiet.

Winston looked at his notes. He had a lot of work ahead of him, but each interview, each piece of evidence, was knitting together the fabric for Stuart's murder. He ordered another coffee and made a list of questions for Lowell. He had an interesting day ahead of him.

Target case file:

In the picturesque world of paragliding, hidden secrets tumble as Detective Winston investigates the brutal hatchet murder of Travis, with only Bryan and Everett in the center of the storm.

Winston walked along the clear lines set up around the paragliding site, his head pounding from the sheer absurdity and gruesomeness of the case. Travis, found dead, his face cleaved into an unfamiliar version of the joy-filled man he was known to be.

There was a suspect that piqued Winston's interest, Bryan. Known all around town for his cookery, especially for his handy use of a hatchet while chopping the hardest of ingredients, sharpened meticulously before each use. Bryan could frequently be seen by town residents, unloading boxes from his delivery truck into his city home, often containing specialized cooking equipment that he personally ordered for home delivery. Further, several witnesses had seen him unloading an array of boxes from his truck into this secluded cabin. Winston learned that Bryan had an insatiable thirst for ensuring his kitchen was bursting with the latest culinary tools. 

"Bryan, what were you doing driving up to this lonely cabin the other day? Delivering more of your tools?" Winston asked him, taking a seat across from Bryan.

"Well, detective, I was just bringin' up some of my cookin' tools. I've been doin' a lot of grilling up here recently," Bryan stuttered, his eyes nervously darted.

"Hatchets for food preparation, huh? That sure is an interesting hobby, Bryan." Winston mentioned. He recalled seeing Bryan the previous day, honing the edge of his hatchet with precision.

"Yes, sir. It's been tradition since when I was a teen. I used to participate lots in hatchet throwin' competitions, you see," Bryan said, his eyes now safely back on Winston, the color slowly draining as he spoke.

Interesting, Winston thought. "Tell me, Bryan. Were Travis's pranks bothering you? Those about you dipping into the petty cash?"

Bryan hesitated for a moment, weighing his words. "About all of his mockery... it's been tough," Bryan said, avoiding Winston's gaze.  "He's been parading around, telling everyone that I've been stealing. He even found a way to publicize I've been dipping into our petty cash."

Winston nodded, trying not to show his surprise. Travis, that jolly, carefree soul resorting to humiliation and accusations? Hard to believe.

"Seems like you've been quite worried about jail, huh, Bryan? Aren't you scared of these accusations?"

"Y-yes... I... I can't go to jail, detective. That’s my worst nightmare, I ..." Bryan faltered, his hand instinctively brushing over his jeans where Winston could spot the handle of his sharpened hatchet, just peeking out, its shine all too prominent.

Winston settled in at his desk, running his fingers over the cold, metallic edges of the woodworking tools that lay strewn across his workspace. They were in evidence bags, cataloged meticulously. A particular hatchet caught his eye, one that lab results had confirmed as the murder weapon. It belonged to Everett, who managed his own private collection of woodworking tools.

Everett, a curator with a keen interest in woodworking, worked at a museum dedicated to the craft. His tools, his museum job, the woodworking... along with these, evidence bags with Everett's paragliding equipment caught Winston's eye. They were marked as found at the murder site, logged and stored.

Deviating from his thoughts about woodworking, Winston began browsing through the case profiles scrolling across his screen.

Travis, the victim, was a paragliding aficionado who had recently earned an international award within the sport—a revered distinction that Everett had also vied for failing to clinch. It seemed Everett struggled for the same acclaim, without much luck. 

Everett's paragliding equipment, now part of the collected evidence from the murder site, was a strong indictor. This was where Travis had met his end. Coincidently the same place where a paragliding event was held that day. 

Straightening up and pocketing his notebook, Winston decided to pay a visit to Everett at the museum.

Whilst there, he noticed Everett skilfully fashioning a piece of wood into a bird’s wing. Maybe it was the context, but it struck him the resemblance it bore to a paraglider's wing.

“Detective Winston,” Everett greeted him, offering a firm, rugged handshake. “Care for a tour?”

Winston declined the offer. “I hear you and Travis were at the same paragliding meetup that day,” Winston started with a nonchalant shrug of his shoulders.

Everett, with a somber nod, confirmed his attendance at said meetup. He muttered something about always being in Travis’ shadow, causing Winston to raise his brow in intrigue.

Before leaving the museum, he waved down a few visitors, asking if they also shared an interest in paragliding. To his surprise, all of them recalled seeing Everett’s vehicle parked at the site of the meetup that day, matching the timings of the murder deeds.

With the image of the hatchet from Everett's collection - the very one identified as the murder weapon - Everett's paragliding gear found at the crime scene, and the chilling timeline coming together, Winston stepped back into the early evening humidity, a new sense of the suspect's world giving weight to his thoughts. But, those dots could wait for another day to connect. For now, it was time to head back to the precinct.

context:
Background files from related investigations (some may be irrelevant):

In a shocking twist of events, Faith has been gruesomely murdered by a lawnmower in her own kitchen and now, Detective Winston must unravel the tangled web of suspicion entangling Clyde and Paul.

Detective Winston strolled into the barber shop, glancing casually around at the collections of stuffed animals that peppered the shop floor. In the very middle of the shop was an imposing stuffed grizzly bear, imposing its dead presence on the area.

Paul was busy with a customer, chatting away about the rare bird species in the case next to the register. The customer, just one of many who had complained about Paul's excessive taxidermy talks, looked painfully bored, his eyes glazed over as Paul prattled on about the bird's curved beak, delicately preserved feathers and where he had obtained such a unique specimen.

Winston leaned by the counter and asked Paul, nonchalantly, "Do you do the occasional yard work in between haircuts?" 

"All the time," Paul responded, finishing up with the disgruntled customer and turning to Winston, not pausing his monologue about another piece of taxidermy. "Yard work helps to make ends meet. I was actually at Faith's place just before...well, you know. I even had access to her kitchen whenever I needed a glass of water."

That seemed to shut him up momentarily, a somber silence filling the barbershop. Winston looked at him, intrigued. 

"It's none of my business, Paul, but I heard your barbershop's been on the rocks lately. Times are tough, huh? Even heard you had to borrow from some loan sharks.", he tried to sound casual.

"Yeah, it's been rough. Lost a few customers, owe some money here and there," Paul’s gaze wandered to the floor, swallowed by the fear of the loan shark's due date.

Winston looked around and made an offhand remark. "Maybe all this taxidermy is scaring them off?"

Paul defended his role, "People don't understand! It's an art." His placid face turned dark, "And nowadays people don’t understand art."

A minute passed before he asked, "Can I use your bathroom, Paul?"

"Sure, Detective, right through that door and to the left.", he said, his gaze falling onto a corner of the shop. 

He let himself into the bathroom, noticing its cleanliness. Paul was meticulous, that was clear. 

As he left, he asked if he could see the papers for Faith's insurance policy. 

"Why?" Paul’s face tensed up at the question. 

"Just routine procedure, Paul." Winston lied.

Paul hesitated before conceding, and then he handed over the papers. Winston skimmed through them, taking a mental note of the surprisingly high coverage and finding that Paul was indeed listed as the sole beneficiary.

Looking straight into Paul's eyes he finally said, "You know, Paul, sometimes it pays to be the policy holder’s primary beneficiary."

Paul looked back at him, pale, but with a composed poker face as he uttered his last denial of the day, "I had nothing to do with Faith’s death, Detective Winston.”

Winston found himself examining a scene in Faith's kitchen, evidence strewn everywhere he looked. He took backward steps, tripping and almost falling on an oddly placed lawnmower at the end of the room. The heavy machine was terribly out of place and hinted at a violent use he found hard to reconcile with the peaceful intent for which it was designed; surely, only someone accustomed to wielding weapons could have wielded it so. 

"Since when has gardening become an indoor activity?" He muttered under his breath, the strange possibility of the lawnmower having been used as a murder weapon intriguing him.

A neighborhood visitor claimed they spotted Clyde, a man whose name popped up frequently during interviews, in Faith's kitchen at the time of the murder. His visit raised suspicions as Faith's husband, Greg, was out of town.

Clyde had just been recently subjected to a publicly organized demotion in his military profession, an event planned by Faith herself. This was a peculiar twist instead of an expected promotion. The profound humiliation Clyde underwent was palpable. Faith didn't just demote him; she ridiculed his past failures in front of friends and colleagues. 

Then Winston found Clyde in his backyard, tirelessly mowing his large lawn. Given his military background, the sight of him comfortably handling the heavy gardening equipment was no surprise. Clad in an army green tank top and dirt smeared jeans, he resembled a typical middle-aged soldier.

"I hear you were out here mowing your lawn yesterday as well," Winston ventured, trying to sound casual.

Clyde simply nodded, "It takes a while, you see. Large lawn and all."

They chatted about his daily chores, Clyde even admitted his preference for maintaining his own lawn. As they spoke of his military background, Clyde shared that he had extensive training in handling various types of weapons and machinery. The mention of this made Winston think of the misplaced lawnmower at Faith's house. 

As the subject shifted towards the night of the murder, Clyde confessed knowing Greg would be away. There was an eerie ease in which he knew about Faith's daily routine, which would have left her alone in the kitchen.

"It was an open secret. Faith loved to bake, known to everyone in the neighborhood," Clyde said, his tone devoid of any resentment.

Winston, before he left, broached the topic of his demotion ceremony. A grimace appeared on Clyde's face at the mention of Faith's sly ploy during his promotion.

"That was... regrettable," he muttered, "Faith had her fun ridiculing me. I swore I would get even for such humiliation."

As Winston reached for the gate, Clyde, playing with the freshly mowed grass, added, "Detective, she didn't just embarrass me, she made it personal. That day will forever be etched in my memory."

Driving back downtown, Winston pondered over the circumstances surrounding Faith's unexpected demise and the uncanny presence of a lawnmower.

In the unsettling calm of the zoo, the peculiar death of Walter by a nail gun sets Detective Winston on a challenging trail of clues, with Glenn and Dennis as prime suspects.

Winston exhaled a stream of smoke as he looked over his notes once more. There were five previous sightings of a man at the local zoo, groceries in hand, and each and every one of them connected to one individual - Glenn. He also found a receipt from the grocery store where Glenn works, it was a purchase for nails specifically for a nail gun.

Remembering a recent eyewitness report of a man on the day of the murder, Winston recalled the description of a man being similar to Glenn, who was spotted carrying a bulky tool bag. 

Winston found Glenn at his place of work. Here, he observed Glenn greeting customers by different names, which sent his antenna up. This detail was also mentioned by Glenn's co-workers who noticed the different names on the rota and found it strange.

Glenn, slightly bulky and distractedly stacking shelves, worked in the same grocery store. Curiously, he made a habit of filling out the work schedule with different names each week, a point his coworkers found as peculiar as Winston did.

The notes also mentioned that Glenn was a troubleshooter. Last winter, instead of hiring a professional, he fixed his leaky roof himself. The nails he bought earlier from the store were for this job, but no nail gun. He had to buy them from elsewhere because the store didn't sell those.

"Glenn?" Winston called out, getting the clerk's attention. Glenn turned, his round face projecting innocence.

"Can I help you?" He replied, offering Winston a smile.

"Winston Phillips, homicide," he introduced himself, flashing his badge briefly.

"Has there, uh, been a murder or something?" Glenn asked, feigning obliviousness.

"You could say that," Winston confirmed, "Could I ask where you were yesterday, Glenn?"

Glenn paused, scratching the back of his head before answering, "Took my little girl to the zoo. We've got a membership there. We always watch the monkeys get fed, it's always at the same time."

Winston's eyebrow lifted slightly. This matches the eyewitness reports placing Glenn at the zoo that day, and another reporting a bulky blue bag on his person.

"A tool bag to the zoo, Glenn?" Winston raised the question.

Glenn’s smile started to fade, "I usually carry it around with me for work, it's got all my tools." He said, a flicker of unease in his eyes, "In case I need them, you know."

Winston found these elements forming a clear image, but he knew better than to impress suspicion where it wasn't explicitly warranted. He would need more. More conversations, more observations, and more unearthing of Glenn’s peculiar behaviours.

Detective Winston brushed crumbs of his sandwich onto his pile of case files. His latest, involving a man named Walter, was proving rather intriguing. Walter had been involved in some questionable business deals... to put it mildly. An interesting detail in all this was that Walter's murder had occurred during an excursion to the local zoo.

Winston squinted his eyes at the witness statement in front of him, given by the key character in this tragedy, a man named Dennis. Dennis had been living with Walter as a foster son and had been a reluctant observer to Walter's illegal doings. He'd had a fear of Walter that was believable in its intensity. His words stuttered and shook on the page as he described how Walter threatened him with dire consequences.

Winston grabbed his keys and headed out to meet with Dennis at his worksite, the lad worked construction, a fact confirmed by Winston's preliminary check.

Approaching the site, Winston saw Dennis working with a nail gun, a tool that looked like a second skin on the young man's hand. Winston could see the professional ease of Dennis wielding the heavy tool and hit his targets with precision.

"Good afternoon, Dennis," Winston greeted him. The young man paused and turned towards him, his face a flicker of honest surprise. "Oh, hi, detective", he replied.

"Dennis", Winston started, "Can you confirm that Walter had invited you to the zoo that day?"

A chill ran over Dennis's face as he replied, "Yes, that's correct."

"Do you often go to the zoo?"

The young man got a far-off look in his eyes, "Yeah, we used to go often. Bonding.. they call it.."

"I see," Winston responded," and about your purchase at the hardware store the day before the visit..."

Dennis looked confused, "Yes, I frequently buy supplies for work. That day, it was a box of nails for my nail gun."

Looking around the site party in admiration and part nostalgia, Winston asked, "Work keeps you busy?"

Grinning at that, Dennis said, "It does, detective, but I had a free day... the day Walter died." His voice caught on the last sentence.

"Alright Dennis, thank you for your time", Winston said, turning on his heel to leave.

The zoo itself was Winston's next stop. He noted it was unusually quiet and several areas were deserted. Perfect chance for a murder, he mused, not that Dennis did it. There's plenty yet to uncover.

As he was exiting, Winston's phone buzzed. His latest query results for Dennis had arrived. The lad did visit a hardware store the day before Walter's murder. And the purchase details matched Dennis's account of buying nails for his nail gun.

Winston buckled up in his car and sighed heavily. There was a sense of fear creeping up his spine, not his own but one that belonged to a young construction worker. A troubled foster son. A possible suspect. A probable witness.

In the mystifying quiet of a mosque, Isabella was found lifeless, a nunchaku the lone cause, casting Detective Winston into a whirlwind investigation with suspects Malaysia and Richard at the heart of the mystery.

Detective Winston was in his office, pouring over the facts of the Isabella case. Isabella was a young woman murdered in a mosque with a pair of nunchaku. Her case was sent to him because not only was the method of murder unusual but the strange behavior she'd reported was disconcerting.

Isabella had reported suspicious activity to the authorities, claiming an acquaintance named Malaysia was acting out of sorts. The name Malaysia was ringing alarm bells for Winston. The police had already questioned her regarding a theft, and now, with Isabella's murder, he felt the need to dig deeper.

Winston knocked on the door of Malaysia's small home, case files in hand. She was a hairdresser by trade, known to be a fan of martial arts movies, placing Bruce Lee as her idol, and had a knack for practicing martial arts moves at home. She had purchased nunchaku recently.  

Winston was greeted with a jovial smile when he arrived, and once pleasantries were exchanged, his questions began.

“I noticed a uniform in that bag by your door,” Winston nodded towards the corner of the room. “You do martial arts?”

“Sure do,” she replied cheerfully. “Nothing like a little kick and a punch after a long day, especially after watching a good martial arts movie.”

Winston watched her closely but Malaysia seemed to only speak the truth. “Did you ever take martial arts classes?”

Malaysia chuckled, “Does high school count? I took it for a few years then. I was a Bruce Lee in the making.”

He took a deep breath and continued, “What about your family, Malaysia?” Winston asked, trying to dig into her background. 

Malaysia shrugged. “Well detective, it's as erratic as the weather these days. Speaking of which, I do believe we are in for some rain later today."

Feeling slightly exasperated, Winston decided to prod a bit more. "And your love life, Malaysia?" he asked. 

"Oh, it's like 'Gone With The Wind'," she replied, winking at him. "An epic which suddenly disappears. Like any good movie, wouldn't you agree, Winston?"

He decided to tread lightly. “You ever practice with nunchaku?”

Malaysia’s gaze never wavered, “Oh, sure. Bought a pair recently. They came in handy when Isabella tried taking my TV. Those are some nice detective notes you've got there around a theft, happened a few days ago, isn't it? The police already asked me about those."

As Winston left Malaysia's home, he was left with a feeling of uncertainty. There was much to unravel about this peculiar woman, and he still couldn’t shake off the uneasy feeling of her jovial exterior that hid a string of suspicious facts. Isabella might have been gone, but Winston was determined to uncover the truth for her sake.

Winston eyed the austere environment of the mosque, draped in silence and shadows. As he looked at this deserted place of worship, he thought of the vibrant Isabella, now lying lifeless.

Remembering his conversations with Isabella's friends, he couldn't help but recall them saying how determined she was to escape Richard for good. Isabella's friends had mentioned her to him - how she told them she intended to finally break free from Richard permanently.

He decided to talk to Richard, a local waiter who had been working at the mosque during those deserted, deadly hours that took Isabella's life.

Richard stood by the main entryway, enduring the barrage of lights and unfamiliar faces. Winston recognized him from his not-so-distant encounter with the law - a case of domestic violence involving him and Isabella.

"Evening, Richard," Winston started, extending a friendly hand. "Been working here long?"

"Few months, sir," Richard replied, his voice steady. "Only serve the occasional visitor during the day. I was alone yesterday. No one else was here."

Winston nodded, making a mental note of Richard's presence at the mosque during the time of Isabella's murder. "I've seen you before. A martial arts class, wasn't it?"

Richard's gaze flickered with surprise before he recovered, his professional mask back in place. "Yes. Same class as Isabella."

Winston recalled seeing Richard in that martial arts class, practicing nunchaku - the same weapon that had ended Isabella's life. And not too long ago, he had seen him at the local sports equipment store, purchasing a set of nunchaku.

"Quite a skill you've got there," Winston continued, keeping his voice casual. "Heard you and Isabella trained together."

Richard sighed, his gaze flicked towards the mosque's silent dome. "Yeah, we both were there. Couldn't seem to get away from each other.”

"I'm sure," Winston agreed. Neighbors had reported frequently hearing the couple arguing, their quarrels escalating in intensity. "How was Isabella doing?"

Richard paused, his brow furrowed. "She... She was... planning to leave."

"Leave?" Winston asked, knowing that Isabella had finally decided to break free from Richard permanently. She had even confided in her friends about her escape plans and purchased a ticket for a one-way trip out of the country.

"Yes..." Richard's voice was barely audible. "Leave me. Leave everything."

With that, Winston thanked Richard and turned to leave, his thoughts spinning around the tragic tale of Isabella, her life brutally ended in this quiet mosque she had formerly sought peace.
