Background files from related investigations (some may be irrelevant):

In the once tranquil mosque, tragedy struck as Jamal was brutally shot dead, and now it's up to Detective Winston to weave through the tangled web of secrets Mark and Gerald are entwined in.

Winston lingered at the fringes of the mosque's gates, studying the CCTV footage on his portable monitor. He was trying to absorb the details, trying to get a feel of the timeline. The footage showed Mark, a well-known local lawyer, clearly entering the mosque before the murder.

Mark was a regular attendee at the mosque for Friday prayers, and the timestamped security footage reinforced that this day was no different.

With a deep sigh, Winston packed up the monitor and made his way to the local store, where he'd arranged to meet with the store's clerks. He'd heard from the community that the quiet lawyer had been seen buying ammunition there.

The clerks confirmed it. Yes, Mark had been to the store to buy shotgun shells. It wasn’t out of place for Mark, known for his involvement with a myriad of firearm-related cases.

As Winston traveled back to his office, he reflected on the conversation he had earlier with Mark. The attorney was an influential figure in the community and often worked on cases involving firearm charges. His knowledge amassed from representing law enforcement personnel showed in his knowledgeable chatter about firearms. 

In their conversation, Mark's fear was evident. It stemmed from Jamal, the victim, who openly expressed extremist beliefs to the community, causing unease. Mark was tasked with ensuring the safety of many community members, and they’d expressed their worries about Jamal to him clearly.

Upon reaching his office, Winston began to piece together the case. He recalled at the time of the incident, Mark was present at the mosque, taking part in prayers along with the others. And Jamal… was Jamal afraid? Thought Winston. The following days would need more thorough investigation. With the data on his desk, the detective prepared himself to slowly trace his way through truth and deception in the days to come.

Winston found himself parked outside the confines of a building overflowing with culture and history - a Mosque, that now is stained with the gruesome murder of Jamal. The wind threatened to dishevel his hair as he made his way inside, crossing paths with Gerald, a violinist who frequented the same religious establishment.

"Gerald, right?" Winston called over the gusty winds, obtaining the attention of the musician.

"Yes, that's me." Gerald nodded, inspecting his violin case as though he could see through it to its contoured resident within.

"You were seen entering the Mosque at an interesting time by the security tapes, Gerald." Winston stated, keeping his gaze steady upon the man.

"Interesting time, detective?" Gerald raised a questioning brow, "I regularly come here for my prayers around this time."

Nodding, Winston eyed the violin case again, "This—a hobby for you or profession?"

"Profession. It consumes a lot of my time but I wouldn't trade it away for anything else,” Gerald responded, traces of pride crossing his features, as his fingers brushed lightly across the case. "Keeps your fingers nimble, doesn't it?" Winston asked casually.

"Absolutely," Gerald responded, smiling softly, "I suppose you could say they're suited to other delicate tasks too."

Winston's gaze darted back to Gerald's face. "Delicate tasks like...?"

"Oh, anything that requires intricate finger movements I suppose.”

This was the first time in a long time anyone had invoked curiosity in Winston, a pleasant change amidst the tragedy. Before he could indulge in this observation, a glint from a computer screen in the corner caught his eye.

“Is that public?” Winston inclined his head towards the computer.

"Why yes, Detective, it's open to all - centerpiece of this quaint little library corner," Gerald explained, before whispering in a reverential tone, "It's perfect for uninterrupted reading."

"Reading anything interesting?"

"Well, I have been immersing myself in the lives of some outstanding violinists who passed away recently. I find a kind of fascination in death, you know."

"Interesting," Winston simply responded, not daring to let a single emotion cross his face. 

Casually resting his hand on Gerald’s shoulder, Winston asked, “Gerald, do you by chance ever go to the shooting range?” 

“Funny you should ask," he answered casually, "I just bought a shotgun last week.”

“Well then," Winston said in a light tone, "maybe I’ll see you around there.”

With that, he let Gerald get back to his life. Taking one last look around the Mosque, Winston exited the building, his mind already buzzing with the next steps of his investigation.

In the haunting echoes of a cinema hall, Tracy's life was abruptly silenced by the grim stroke of a meat cleaver, leaving Detective Winston grappling with a chilling mystery and two elusive suspects - Nicole and Gloria.

Winston, standing behind the caution tape, looked at the cinema marquee. He allowed the scene to imprint itself in his mind before he would venture inside to inspect the crime scene. A murder at the movies was a rarity. But what was even more unusual was the murder weapon used: a meat cleaver.

Reviewing the details of the case once more, Winston thought about some key players involved. Undeniably traceable was Gloria, a hardcore fan of the rock band 'The Butchers', known by everyone and even herself in interviews, as a groupie. She had also confessed in one such media interaction that she was crazy about taxidermy, a hobby brought to life in her house.

Leaving the crime scene, Winston made his way to Gloria's house in the fading evening sun. Upon entering Gloria's home, he found himself in a museum of morbid curiosity. From the ceiling to the floor, taxidermied animals filled the house with glassy eyes reflecting in the dim light, a testimony to her hobby.

Among her collection, he noticed a recent addition - a rare bird, its exotic colors momentarily catching his gaze. Bob, the local bird dealer, had already confirmed its purchase by Gloria.

Winston inquired about her whereabouts the previous night.

"Well, I was at the movie premiere, of course," Gloria responded. "I, along with Tracy, went to the double event. The Butchers premiered their new music video during the movie. And well, you couldn't expect me to miss that, now could you? I follow every event they put up and not just because I'm a fan. Because I am in love with the lead singer, and yes I'm saying it."

Winston let the information sink in.

"Well... isn't it true that Tracy, the victim, was planning to go public with an affair?" Winston asked.

A momentary flicker passed in Gloria's eyes. "Yes... I know about that," Gloria confessed. "She was dating the lead singer, the poor man. She wanted to reveal everything, destroy everything."

With that, Winston left Gloria's house with more questions buzzing in his head. He got back into his car, piecing together the intricate web of clues this case held. The concert that the Butchers were supposed to play after the movie was now going to be remembered for all the wrong reasons.

Deep in thought, Winston flipped through the photographs of the movie theatre crime scene, when his partner handed him an envelope. A DVD from the theatre's CCTV records, witnessing every unscripted moment at the theatre that did double-duty, not just as a place to showcase films, but also as a distinctive setting for unorthodox weddings, just like the one Tracy had intended to have. Eyewitnesses at the scene confirmed Nicole's presence at the theatre during the murder. The records would be viewed later.

His current priority was to interrogate Nicole, the esteemed wedding planner, the woman whose entire reputation and business were built on her success in this field. By an unfortunate coincidence, she had been at the theatre when Tracy was murdered, not just as a cinema enthusiast, but as the individual orchestrating Tracy's movie-themed wedding at the same theatre.

"Nice place you've got here," Winston observed as he ventured into Nicole's office, its grandeur coupled with an array of movie posters illustrating her success in planning film-themed weddings.

"Well, Detective, events won't plan themselves," Nicole said, with a small, tight smile. "Tracy hired me for one of my elaborate movie-themed weddings. She was drawn to the unusual."

Surveying the space, he noticed it was not only amassed with wedding supplies but also held a vast array of kitchen equipment. Nicole had been responsible for preparing the meat at several events as evident from the professional cleavers that took center stage amongst the kitchenware. One of them catching his eye; a meat cleaver.

"On food responsibility as well?" Winston asked.

"Indeed. Delivering comprehensive experiences is the goal. Every specification matters, including the banquet," Nicole imparted. "My past as a culinary student till being a wedding planner helped shape that. I even received professional training in meat preparation."

"Interesting," Winston murmured, quickly connecting two points - Nicole's past culinary training and Tracy's murder weapon, a meat cleaver.

"Rumor has it that you made a considerable blunder at Tracy's wedding," Winston broached. "Word on the street is that Tracy was so embarrassed she was looking to file a malpractice suit against you.”

"A minor miscalculation. No one is perfect, detective. However, Tracy blew it out of proportion," Nicole responded, her face growing somber.

Observing her seemingly unflustered demeanor, Winston mused on her case. He knew a large scale malpractice suit could irreparably harm a professional's reputation. For someone like Nicole whose entire business relied on her successful track record as a wedding planner, it could be a fateful blow. 

Before confronting her head-on, he decided to examine the perspectives of the eyewitnesses and the CCTV footage. His eyes strayed to the cold, gleaming steel of the meat cleaver amidst Nicole's kitchen equipment. This reminded him of Tracy, and he made himself a promise: he would find justice for her.

Target case file:

In a bustling office, a mundane bottle of bleach becomes a lethal weapon, leading to the chilling murder of Murray; it's up to the sharp-minded Detective Winston to navigate through a web of deceit spun by Chris and Gloria, the enigmatic suspects.

The rain was lightly tapping against the window of Detective Winston's office as he examined his notes. His latest case involved a peculiar victim, Murray, who was fond of working alone during the twilight hours in his office. The cause of death was a strange one - bleach ingestion.

After nightfall, Winston's steps echoed in the office building as he sought out his next interviewee. Emerging from a nondescript door labelled "Rehearsal", the sound of dancers practicing halted abruptly. Winston found himself amongst Gloria's dominion.

“Ms. Gloria, could I have a moment of your time?” Winston asked, interrupting her choreography.

“Every second counts, Detective... My rehearsals always seem to go overtime,” Gloria replied, her voice resounding in the empty practice space. Around her, a set of costumes lined the room, each one carefully cleaned. Gloria had a reputation for maintaining the utmost hygiene in her costumes.

Winston remarked, "It's unusual to see a dance studio without a security camera. The owners not concerned about break-ins?"

“Well, they leave matters of security to us... How could I help, Detective?” Gloria pushed aside her rehearsal props, which included a curious bleach bottle among her personal belongings, providing Winston a chair in her living quarters in the rehearsal building. Given her late-night practices, she had repurposed a portion of the room to serve as her personal living space.

In her living space, an enormous filing cabinet stood imposingly, filled to the brim with newspaper clippings. Winston could tell she was fond of keeping up with recent events. Also, the sheer size of the cabinet suggested it might be Gloria’s version of a living room.

"I see you have a large filing cabinet in your living quarters, Gloria. That’s quite full of newspaper clippings." Winston commented, pointing to the open drawer.

"Ah, Detective, I like to stay informed... I make it a point to read through every obituary in the early morning. A peculiar morning ritual, I know...," Gloria replied, confirming her subscription to every local newspaper.

"You certainly seem to research chemicals, too,” Winston observed, his eye having been caught by the organized array of chemical notations and formulas that were punctuating her choreography notes.

“Absolutely," Gloria animatedly replied, quickly adding, "For example, bleach is highly toxic when ingested. It's commonly used for maintaining the hygiene of the costumes.” 

Winston stood up to leave, thanking Gloria for her time. "So do you use this office year-round?"

"No, only for late-night practices. And I believe Murray also preferred afterhours here," Gloria offered.

"Thank you for your time, Gloria."

“Detective, are you sure you have all the information you need?” Gloria asked, escorting him to the door.

“I believe I do. I’ll be in touch,” Winston nodded, stepping back out into the dim-lit alley.

Winston sat in the hard plastic chair outside the office of Chris, the coach of the office's intramural sports leagues. The location seemed like an unlikely place for a murder, but Murray had indeed collapsed dead in his office several buildings over from ingesting a poisonous substance, a terrible surprise considering Murray typically avoided the recreational facilities of the office.

The door cracked open, and Chris invited Winston in. The office was small but spacious enough to hold stacks of sports equipment, training manuals and a variety of cleaning agents that he included as part of his coaching supplies - everything from towels to a close-to-empty bottle of bleach. Winston looked at the bleach and couldn't help but recollect the unfortunate death of Murray, caused by poison.

The two men sat on either side of the desk cluttered with paper-work and game plans. "Murray?" Chris grimaced as he spoke out the name of the victim, a surprising response from an individual not typically associated with the inter-office politics.

Winston cleared his throat, initiating the conversation. "When did you last see him, Chris?"

"Funny you'd ask. Just yesterday, in his office. Over a decision in the final game, you know." Chris's voice grew noticeably cooler.

Winston recalled the chatter at the water-cooler about last week's defeat in the championship game. The stakes high, the loss did not sit well with the team or Chris, as Winston observed from the stern look on the coach's face. There had been confrontations, Winston had heard, and the echo of an argument -- Murray's decision suddenly seemed to favor the rival team.

"Everyone was... upset," Winston found the right word, "about the decision. The last match was important, wasn't it?"

"More than just a game, wasn’t it Detective?" Chris's evasive reply wrapped around his rising passion for the job. The loss was more personal, Winston noted.

“You’re here during the day, right?” Winston asked, looking for a confirmation.

“Yes, sir. My coaching matches the office's regular hours,” Chris replied.

“Your duties - it must be more than throwing balls and yelling at players.” It was Winston’s turn to lighten up the mood.

“Funny, Detect. I’m responsible for equipment and supply maintenance. And trust me, yanking up fifty-pound weights and keeping the towels and bottles clean and safe - it ain’t no walk in the park.”

"Safe? Like using cleaning products perhaps,” Winston stated, looking right at the supplies Chris kept in his office.

“Sure. You never know when something spills. Have to keep it all clean and safe," Chris echoed.

Winston recollected an incident from the past where a young office athlete under Chris's coaching had ingested cleaning fluid, mistaken for water no less, and had an unpleasantly grim hospital visit. The echo of that incident reverberating in the present, with Murray's poisoning almost felt like a devious pattern, thought Winston.

"Wouldn’t want another upset tummies, would we?” Winston rose from the chair, leaving Chris with a thoughtful stare.

"No, we wouldn’t, Detective."

Winston left the office, running over the conversation in his mind as he remembered the empty bottle of bleach in the corner of Chris’s office. There was certainly more to uncover; the echoes of past and present were too loud to ignore.

In the quiet tranquility of the city park, Bria's life was abruptly ended with a hatchet, leaving Detective Winston with two prime suspects - Serenity and Naomi.

Winston never loved parks, even when he was a kid. But nevertheless he walked through the city park, talking with some locals there on their morning strolls. He was investigating the death of a young woman, Bria, found dead—yes, here—in these park grounds days before.

His steps took him to the park’s community center, a hub that also served as a point of supply for the various camps around the city. The center stored tools such as hatchets for outdoor activities, usually deployed during camping. He made his way to the office of Naomi, an intern there working specifically with these tools. Naomi taught camping skills not only at the center but also at the camps. She taught how to swing a hatchet, how to build a fire, and overall, how to survive in the wilderness.

Winston knocked, and Naomi opened the door. Winston noticed bandages on her hands.

“Hello, Naomi,” Winston said, “I understand that you knew Bria?”

“Yes,” she said, “We knew each other. She… she was very violent towards me.”

“Violent how?”

“She, uhm… she assaulted me. Several times. I reported her violent behavior multiple times to the police. I was even granted a restraining order against her... at least I had…”

The words hung in the air. “I was even hospitalized once because of her. All the time, I felt jeopardized by her continuous attacks” 

“And Bria, she was here the day she was murdered?”

“I was told she was planning to be here that day, yes. On the same day, I was leading an outdoor skills class. And it was indeed a strange coincidence, I was teaching people how to use a hatchet for chopping wood.”

“A coincidence,” Winston repeated, looking at the bandages on Naomi’s hands again. Then, without a word more, Winston turned and left. He had more people to talk to, and more questions to ask.

Winston flicked his cigarette lighter close, producing a small gust of smoke. The case was still in its initial stages, but he had already pieced together some revealing tidbits. He scrawled on the desk all he knew about a woman named Serenity - the prime suspect.

He'd first heard about her from a group who camped locally. It was their regular outing spot, they'd told him. "Serenity is always with us.. always got her hatchet in tow. We've seen her use it - she knows what she's doing," they'd mentioned while sharing tales of their outings.

Winston had kept the group to the side and decided to pay a visit to Serenity's home. As he'd approached her home, he'd noticed something unusual about her - her fascination with bugs. Every room was filled with display cases containing various insects, some of them rarely seen in their town. He'd even observed several of those he recognized to be rare and expensive. From what he could see, she had made significant investments to procure and preserve her insect collection, hinting at her large expenses in preserving the rare insects.

Her routine was also centered around these creatures. Apparently, she frequented the library often, particularly the entomology section. In fact, the library's records showed that she had checked out several books on insects.

What added to all this was a piece of evidence that Winston couldn't shake off - a letter from the victim. It had been addressed to Serenity, with Bria explicitly mentioning her intentions to testify. The letter revealed Bria's possession of damaging information regarding Serenity's singular, and highly illegal, practices in insect collection and preservation.

As he visited the library for some more information, a clerk had passed him an interesting insight. "That girl Serenity? Always in the insect section – with her hatchet, too. Sharpens it while reading, she does."

Winston returned to his table with his thoughts. As he flipped through the pages of notes, he came upon a second revelation about Serenity's newfound predicament. After corroborating with several of Bria's friends, Winston learned that Bria had confided in them about her decision to testify against Serenity. The information Bria had was extremely serious, which could lead to dire consequences for Serenity.

Strengthening his suspicion was one piece of evidence echoing in his mind – a hatchet, freshly used and confiscated from Serenity that eerily matched the deadly weapon at the crime scene. Forensic reports confirmed that the blood and ridges of the hatchet were an exact match to the murder weapon at park, tightening his grip on Serenity. Winston could see the connecting dots, but the fear of jumping to conclusions had his caution wobbling on a thin thread.

The day may have ended, but the case had only just begun.

In the heart of a rainforest, Peyton's life was brutally ended with a hatchet, pulling grizzled Detective Winston into a twisted web of deceit featuring suspects Bruce and Norris.

Winston took a careful look at the grim scene. The deceased, Peyton, was found with a gruesome hatchet wound deep in the heart of the rainforest.

While sorting through the information at hand, Winston recalled a bit of crucial info about the suspect - Bruce, Peyton's partner in their shared illicit business. Bruce had mentioned that the day Peyton was found, he had been alone in the rainforest. A rumored confession and potential surrender by Peyton, and the stolen goods Peyton found stashed away, kept echoing in Winston's mind.

As the detective stepped away from the lamenting scene, he called in to schedule an interview with the partner, Bruce. He was known to visit the rainforest often, sometimes for solitude, sometimes under the guise of his illicit activities.

Meeting Bruce at the entrance to the rainforest the following day, Winston sized him up. Nothing about his demeanor suggested guilt. Despite fearing the legal consequences of his actions, there was a calm about Bruce. For someone raised in the rainforest, he seemed one with the environment, he was comfortable in it.

Winston asked Bruce about his usual activities in his favorite retreat, prompting him to say, "I usually just like to be alone here, sir. A few chops here and there with my hatchet helps maintain the paths and keeps me busy."

Bruce’s answer inclined Winston to inquire, “And where is this hatchet now?” 

With a frown, Bruce replied, “I couldn’t find it today, sir. I usually keep it well maintained and in its usual spot.”

Their talk was interrupted by a passerby, jogging down a path. After briefly chatting about the area and visitor trends they noticed, the jogger mentioned that they hadn't seen anyone else in the rainforest that particular day, let alone someone leaving. The jogger left. Bruce turned back to Winston and shared, "Nobody usually notices me here, even when leaving the rainforest. It’s quite secluded.”

The thought of Peyton's gruesome death by the hatchet wound came back to Winston's mind. He abruptly thanked Bruce for his time and walked away.

The rainforest echoed with the weighted silence of the untold, and, as Winston ventured back to the city, a haunting thought lingered. The quiet, confident Bruce, with his missing hatchet, was confirmed to have been alone the last day Peyton was seen alive, and as the jogger had informed, unseen when he left the rainforest; the same day Peyton died.

Winston examined the manifest from Norris's ferry one final time. It matched up with what he already knew: Peyton had indeed been aboard Norris's ferry on the day he was killed. Winston took one last look at the document before folding it and tucking it away into his coat pocket.

Norris, the ferry captain, had a reputation amongst the barflies at his favorite local watering hole. They'd often overheard him detailing possibly too realistic scenes from the books they discussed at his thriller murder novel themed book club. Norris would get into specifics that made the members uncomfortable, his eyes often taking on an excited shine while he spoke of these gruesome and too-detailed-to-be-fiction murder scenes.

Tapping his notepad with a worn-down pen, Winston glanced up as Norris approached. Clad in his usual captain's garb and appearing a bit rough around the edges from years of running the ferry. Norris acted as the key traveling back and forth to the local rainforest, the last known place Peyton was seen alive.

"Captain Norris?" Winston asked, even though he already knew the answer. Norris nodded in confirmation, his steady gaze meeting Winston's. "Been doing this job for years," Norris said, a hint of pride reflected in his voice.

"It's a sturdy vessel you have," Winston commented as he gestured towards the ferry, his eyes landing on a standalone toolbox propped up near the bow. One item in particular stood out from the rest— a hatchet, well-used and worn, clear evidence of its frequent use in the maintenance of the ship under Norris's experienced hands.

"Ah, yes. That's Gertrude," Norris responded, referencing the hatchet, drawing Winston's attention back to him. Considering he was the only ferry giving rides to that rainforest, it was crucial Norris kept the ferry in good shape.

Winston then redirected the conversation, "We have a record of a Peyton. Took your ferry to the rainforest on the day of the murder. Anything you recall?"

Norris took a moment to recall, his brow furrowing in concentration. "Hmm... Peyton? Yeah, sure. He was one of my passengers that day."

After a few more hours of questioning, Winston returned to his squad car. The rainforest still lay heavy in his mind, and Peyton was a name he would not forget. But for now, he had everything he could glean from Norris, the ferry captain. His path forward would have to reveal itself in time.

When the silver screen flickered with an unexpected explosion, claiming the life of innocent Chloe, seasoned Detective Winston stepped in to unravel the deadly scandal entwining suspects Ruby and Roscoe.

Despite the night's residue of tobacco clinging to his garment, Detective Winston took a deep inhale as he approached Ruby. He pulled out a crumpled picture of Chloe from his pocket and sighed, replaying the explosion at the movie theatre over and over in his mind, as well as the image of Jake, the man he's spotted Chloe with on numerous clandestine dates.

"Ruby," he began. His voice was low and weary. "I understand that you and Chloe had planned a sister-courtship to the movies last night."

A flicker of surprise crossed Ruby's face. "Why, yes. Chloe wanted to see that new film, The Scarlet Phoenix. We enjoyed a night at the theater till the very end. Nobody else entered or left the theater during our stay - it was just us."

"Interesting," muttered Winston. "And there were eyewitnesses confirming that you were the last person seen with Chloe?" 

"Yes," said Ruby hesitatingly,"We departed together."

"Interesting," muttered Winston, making no further comment. Instead, he considered the reported vision of Ruby seeing Chloe kissing another man. Another man who turned out to be Jake.

"I understand that you might have feelings for Jake. Is that right?" Winston questioned, watching Ruby carefully.

Ruby hesitated, playing with the locket around her neck. “Yes, I suppose that's true,” she admitted, but never meeting his gaze.

The detective changed the angle of the conversation. “I've heard tales about your psychic abilities, Ruby. You tend to see dangerous things. Your visions included dreadful bomb scenarios back when you were in the military, right?”

"I've had visions," Ruby replied defensively. "Visions are often ambiguous. They can symbolize various scenarios. I did see Chloe, Chloe kissing another man... Jake. And yes, during my service, I’ve seen how war and destruction unfold, even how to use grenades."

"I can imagine," Winston said, thinking to himself. Connecting the dots, he continued, "Did you know that Jake and Chloe were secretly seeing each other?"

Ruby's apprehension told Winston everything he needed to know. "Yes, I knew. Chloe told me about it," she said, her face growing pale.

"Did you also stay behind after the movie, in the theatre?" Winston asked, looking at Ruby sternly.

"We both enjoyed the ending credits music, so we stayed till the end. I distinctly remember walking out of the theatre last night, but... alone," Ruby said, hinting at her absence following the movie's completion.

Winston allowed a moment's pause before continuing on. "Ruby, where did you go after the movie ended?"

"I went to my brother's house," Ruby's reply was swift, a touch too swift.

Winston blinked, remembering her brother's notorious reputation as an arms dealer, and Ruby's own military background. "That's... convenient."

"I suppose it is," Ruby replied quietly, eyes fixed on the policeman's tired, yet zealous gaze. The meeting was concluded with that, leaving Winston with the chilling evening wind and another lead in Chloe's puzzling demise.

Winston glanced at the movie ticket stub Roscoe held, noting that it was for the same film as Chloe. He squinted at Roscoe, who was a respected astrophysicist and dedicated military officer, but his current disheveled appearance suggested a disconnect. 

"You were here at the theatre when the event happened, then?" Winston asked, gesturing at the ticket. Roscoe was indeed there before the movie started, now confirmed by the timing on his ticket. 

A confirmed nod came from Roscoe, who avoided meeting Winston’s gaze. "Yeah, I was here. Same movie as her." His voice dropped lower. "When the incident occurred during the movie screening. Chloe... She didn't make it."

Winston hesitated, knowing Chloe's death wasn't the only thing he needed to discuss today. Throughout their conversation, Winston noticed a limp in Roscoe's step, bruises, and a sharp wince when he moved a certain way. "Looks like you've got some injuries there," Winston remarked casually. 

Though he spoke offhandedly, Roscoe was quick to brush it off, often changing the subject when questioned about his injuries, which drew Winston’s attention. More so than before, Winston observed, people tended to notice when someone was deliberately avoiding a topic.

Trying not to push too far, Winston paused momentarily - but then he remembered the drug bag found in Roscoe’s possession at the theater. He recalled a report from resident neighbors as well, Mr. & Mrs. Davenport, stating that they've often seen Roscoe limping into his apartment late in the night, disheveled and pained. Further arousing suspicion was the doorman’s testimony, reporting a similar disheveled state during the late-night arrivals.

Remaining cognizant of the consequences to Roscoe’s military career if he were to be caught using drugs, Winston pressed on, "Roscoe, I've heard you've been behaviorally inconsistent at work lately. And there’s the matter of the confiscated drug bag. Do you understand the negative implications this could have for your military career?"

Roscoe visibly flinched. His demeanor took on a nervous edge, scratching his arm as it often did when he felt cornered. Winston’s gaze hardened, feeling certain that Roscoe was the name written in secret within Chloe's notebook. The one she intended to report for drug usage.

“I...uh got to use the restroom," Roscoe stammered before rushing off, undoubtedly the effects of the drugs kicking in.

Winston decided to follow, needing more answers. Was Roscoe the reason behind Chloe's demise? Was this why he'd jeopardize a promising military career with drug addiction? With renewed determination, Winston set off after him.

As Winston neared the restroom, he was eerily reminded of the nearly empty crime scene — a movie theatre mid-showing. He shuddered at the thought of the panic that ensued when the grenade went off during the screening.

But there was no time for that now, he had a suspect to confront.

In an adrenaline inducing bungee jumping site, Mack's thrill-seeking adventure came to a gruesome end by a nunchaku; now, it's up to Detective Winston to unravel the deadly secrets between Mackenzie and Ana.

Winston sat quietly in an unmarked Ford, parked a block away from Mackenzie's downtown apartment building. He observed Mackenzie through his binoculars, watching closely as they hastily unlocked their front door. It had been a long day at the office for Mackenzie and, like clockwork, they were seen taking their customary break on a public bench, working on their laptop.

Before long, Mackenzie was seen through the partially closed blinds of their apartment, sitting at their desk with their laptop open. They had just returned from a local cyber security meetup, a reality Winston discovered after following Mackenzie to the event later that evening. As Winston watched, they shifted their body and their eyes darted around, Winston duly noted on Mackenzie's apparent concern for online privacy.

"Interesting," Winston thought, while making a mental note to do some research on further cyber security meetups occurring in the vicinity.

The next morning, Winston watched Mackenzie walk out of a martial arts training center. As Mackenzie stopped to say goodbye to their instructor, Winston quickly snapped a photo on his phone. In the picture, Winston could clearly see Mackenzie practicing techniques with the unmistakable form of Mackenzie's sturdy nunchaku resting in the backdrop. This gave Winston a clue that his martial arts training includes nunchaku techniques.

Winston's interest peaked further when he followed Mackenzie to a local shop where they were seen purchasing a new set of nunchaku. Even more intriguing was when they examined a pair of cufflinks on display with a yearning look, cufflinks Winston knew were identical to a pair Mack frequently flaunted around. It appeared Mack had things that Mackenzie also desired.

The investigator decided it was time to pay Mackenzie a visit. He knocked on the apartment door and Mackenzie cautiously invited him in.

Pleasantries were briefly exchanged before Winston's gaze quickly fell on the laptop that was resting by some papers next to an open window.

"You always take this with you to work?" Winston inquired, pointing at the laptop.

"Every day," Mackenzie replied, "I can't leave my work at the office."

"Work goes that well, huh?" Winston probed further. "I hear you were recently ... overlooked for a promotion."

At these words, Mackenzie's expression darkened. "I was the top candidate, you know. It should've been mine. Mack, the new guy, he is nothing compared to me, but he takes it. That promotion, the respect I had. Even those cufflinks I have always wanted, somehow Mack always gets to have them."

Winston nodded, making a mental note of Mackenzie's reaction. They turned the conversation to martial arts and during the chat, Mackenzie unintentionally revealed their prowess with nunchaku.

In a small, hidden compartment in Mackenzie's wardrobe, Winston found the pair of nunchaku that Mackenzie had recently purchased. He swiftly snapped a picture of this evidence before closing the wardrobe.

As the day grew late, Winston thanked Mackenzie for their time and headed out, feeling more certain than ever about the path his investigation was following.

Winston sat in his office, photos of Mack --the bungee jumper found dead-- scattered heartbreakingly across his desk. The lack of clues at the murder site puzzled him, nothing seemed out of place. All he had was an unusual weapon, the nunchaku, not something he’d found at too many crime scenes.

Standing up, he straightened his tie and headed to the shared housing complex of the victim and suspect. Ana Diaz lived here, along with Mack. Ground rules for questioning the suspect were laid out in his mind.

Ana received him with a stoic expression and invited him inside. Her suitcase was unpacked, strewn helter-skelter around the room. She explained she had come back from the bungee jumping site late last night, still in shock about Mack’s murder.

Nunchaku lay on the table. Winston noticed, she explained it as the normal household item of a martial artist. She said she practices martial arts at the same bungee jumping location. 

Asked about their shared occupation, she sighed heavily. “Mack loved it, though," She said, "He was the instigator, insisting everyone take the jump.”

Ana seemed to soften, talking about her faith, her traditions. “Bungee jumping, it's against my beliefs,” she admitted, “but I’d signed up too, expecting some ridicule like always.”

Ridicule. That was a word Winston had already heard before concerning Mack. He asked around, among their friends, everyone said the same, Mack liked to joke, to point fun at beliefs. Especially Ana’s it seemed.

They left together, Ana and Mack, the morning of the murder, people had seen them. Winston asked why, given their strained relationship. Ana shrugged off, her hands trembling. “He wasn’t too bad,” she replied. 

Nobody else was documented at the bungee jumping site that day, only Mack and Ana. It was time to head there. Winston thanked Ana for her time and left, driving straight to the scene. He stared up at the looming diving board, picturing the scene.  

Only two people there that day, Mack and Ana. He looked around, the martial arts practice ground nearby held the last piece. Nunchaku, a common weapon in martial arts practices. He tested one, the weight fitting neatly into his palm while he surveyed the area. This was the scene he needed to piece together.

In the heart of bustling Times Square, Johnny's life was abruptly ended with an unlikely weapon—a trident—and now, Detective Winston must unravel the murky truths hidden behind suspects Jay and Karl.

Winston immersed himself in the bustle of Times Square. The lights always seemed brighter after such a grim event. This used to be where Johnny, a legally adopted son of Jay, and Jay himself celebrated New Year's. However, tonight, their anticipated joint celebration was tarnished with tragedy. Jay was meant to accompany his son tonight, as he always did in previous years. Yet, today, the gaiety was marred by the spilt blood of young Johnny.

Taking silent inventory of the night's events, Winston departed Times Square and headed towards the residence of his unsuspecting suspect, Jay. He received curious glances from the neighbors as he passed by. His presence was quite striking given they were accustomed to seeing the irregular delivery trucks from far-flung places, implying Jay's suspected illegal fishery.

Reaching Jay's estate, Winston was greeted with a spectacle bizarre yet beautiful. Carefully arranged insects, like war trophies, were displayed for all. The place breathed less like an extermination spot and more like an entomologists’ gallery. In their conversation, Jay fervently talked of insects' idiosyncrasies reminiscing often about his entomology degree he pursued in college. It was a knowledge accumulated over the years, he claimed.

Despite such peculiar oddities, something else caught Winston’s attention. Jay's demeanor exhibited an aura of a grieving father who had just lost his child. Every word, every gesture towards Johnny was drenched in fatherly affection. This he observed as he subtly probed into Jay's Times Square hotel booking from that very night shared over their New Year's plans discussion.

Jay confidently produced the confirmation for his hotel reservation, confirming his presence at Times Square, booked for the very night of the murder taking place. He seemed unbothered, almost casual like discussing an ordinary routine, even when Johnny's intention to report his illegal fishery was disclosed. Winston found this revelation stirring. Johnny had confessed to him, and unbelievably, Jay happened to overhear their private conversation revealing Johnny's turn of trust.

The conversation took a turn towards Jay's unusual hobbies, including the exotic delivery trucks that catered to his needs, and the display cases filled with nicely arranged insects. Jay, light-hearted in his response, flirted with anecdotes trailing from his college days.

The air was thick with grief as they remembered Johnny. Loaded with information, Winston pieced together a clear perspective of the suspect. Yet the investigation was far from over. Something hung unanswered, unfinished. As Winston exited Jay's house, silence echoed the unspoken truths left to be discovered.

Winston scrutinized the surroundings of Times Square. It was almost surreal that amidst the clamor and hustle, a murder had taken place here, Johnny's murder. The murder weapon was peculiar, a trident.

Despite the city's innumerable faces, battalions of CCTV cameras, incessantly flashing screens surrounding the quadrant, a witness had spotted Karl here.

Clearing his throat, Winston began his interrogation. "You've been spotted here today Karl, can you explain that?"

The reply came quick, "Yeah, I was here, detective. I come here often."

"You and Johnny had an argument?"

"Yes," Karl nodded, then his face grew grave. "He threatened to go to the police about some documents he'd found. I tried to reason with him,” said Karl, his voice trembling slightly. “But we argued. We argued often. He had a hot temper, and I suspect, mad as hell he was."

People swarmed around like an ongoing carnival, but Winston kept his gaze unwavered on Karl. "You have a soft spot for history, don't you?" Winston ventured.

"Yeah, I love historical weaponry. I've got a nice collection at home," Karl stated somewhat proudly.

Winston knew, his suspicion was correct. The house search had revealed a Trident among Karl's collection of ancient weapons, now confiscated.

"Interesting," he observed. "Used any of them? For fighting or such."

"Tridents... I took some trident fighting lessons last summer," Karl admitted with an awkward laugh.

Strange coincidence, or just an indication of motives, Winston thought. Besides, the trident and Times Square; there was also that heated argument over some documents about his financial misdemeanors.

"Financial misdemeanors," Winston probed.

The look in Karl's eyes revealed something, but he simply shrugged, "Stock market’s a tricky business, detective. Johnny didn't fully understand it."

Winston thanked him for his time and left. City lights illuminated the square. Karl, now successful in stock manipulation, hoped to remain unseen by the police. But Johnny knew, and had discovered evidence of Karl’s illegal activities. Winston had a feeling, the city that never slept would soon reveal its hidden truths.

In the chilling silence of a hockey rink, Marvin's life was brutally ended with a machete, leaving Detective Winston with two elusive suspects: Justin and Frederick.

Winston sifted through the reports on his desk: the hockey rink homicide, the outlandish murder weapon, the victim known as Marvin who was scheduled to play a hockey game that fateful day. His attention fell onto a single name: Justin.

Leaning back in his chair, Winston found his thoughts weaving around Justin's profession—a piercer; an occupation requiring specific tools like needles and, in Justin's unique case, machetes.

He recalled his past dealings with Justin, particularly how he demonstrated a morose disposition after his proposal got rejected. Winston recalled the desperation in Justin's eyes as he recounted his romantic proposal to Marvin's fiancé. Unfortunately for him, the lady chose Marvin over him.

Justin, who had been frequenting Marvin's hockey games, was there again for the scheduled match. When he arrived, he found Justin waiting amidst the empty seats.

"You watched Marvin's hockey game frequently, yeah?" Winston began, staring up at Justin with a curiosity that was intense. Justin's face distorted with pain as he gave a nod in affirmation, silently communicating his reasons for being there the day of the murder.

Winston shifted on his feet and continued, "You were here that day, weren’t you? To watch Marvin play?"

"I came to watch the game, like always. It was just unfortunate what happened," Justin replied, his voice empty of any emotion.

Winston took a moment before continuing, "I have full CCTV footage of you entering the rink at the time of Marvin's scheduled game, and not leaving until an hour after the murder was supposedly committed." 

Pulling out a photo of a distinct, ornate machete from his coat pocket, he asked: "Recognize this? CCTV also shows you carrying a bag into the rink of such size and shape, which could've carried this. And forensics confirmed that this machete, with your piercing studio's distinct engravings, was the murder weapon."

Justin's eyes widened as truthful recognition flashed in them. Winston's next visit would be Justin's piercing parlor.

Justin's piercing studio was like an alternate world. Display cases filled with shiny replicas of machetes were fixed on the walls; a reminder of his unique craft. An odd weapon for a piercer, but it seems it had become Justin's tool of choice. Upon inquiring the staff, he found that only Justin handled these machetes. Furthermore, no other employee had access to them.

His next stop was to Marvin's fiancé, a delicate woman, embodying sorrow and distraught. 

"Justin approached you about not marrying Marvin, didn’t he?" Winston struck a direct chord, to which she only nodded, tears welling up in her eyes.

Following the tiring day of investigation, Winston drove back to the precinct. Entering the rink at the time Marvin was scheduled to play, Justin's presence at the murder site, his connection with the weapon, his relations with the victim and Marvin's fiancé - all confirmed by CCTV and forensic evidence, he had gathered ample information. Now, it was time to piece it all together.

The biting chill at the crime scene did nothing to alleviate the morbid spectacle in front of Winston. Marvin's body, brutally murdered with a machete and left on the icy, hockey rink made for an astonishing scene. 

Marvin was no saint though. Rumors of his volatile behavior had circulated around town for quite some time.

Having gone through the initial inspection of the crime scene, Winston decided to pay Frederick a visit at his spacious residence next to the cemetery. The presence of Frederick's numerous antique machetes at the crime scene was too much of a coincidence to ignore. The man had far too many in his collection for it to go unnoticed. Frederick, in his role as the curator of the local weapons museum, had unrestricted access to a range of armaments. And curiously, Marvin had been killed with a weapon from Frederick's extensive collection.

Upon reaching the house, Winston noticed Frederick fitting the key into the lock of the cemetery gate, signifying his unrestricted access to the nearby graveyard. 

As he walked up to the front porch, he noticed an ominous array of mourning books displayed on a nearby table. He asked about them and Frederick proudly claimed them to be a part of his vast collection documenting rituals from many different cultures.

Upon greeting Frederick, he was immediately shown inside by Frederick's anxious daughter. She was noticeably shaken up from hearing of Marvin's murder, considering that Marvin had recently publicly threatened her. 

Upon hearing that, Frederick's reaction was expected. He was an incredibly protective father and the news visibly upset him. 

Frederick, seeming desperate to change the topic started talking about his travels, elaborating how he was tasked with visiting and studying the weapons and tombs of ancient cultures.

Sensing Frederick's discomfort, Winston decided to leave the conversation there. He observed his surroundings one final time before thanking them for their hospitality and reminding them to stay safe.

As he strolled back to his car, he noted the machete from Frederick's collection stationed in the museum, something he had been specifically overseeing.

In the quiet of a home office, Mackenzie met a fiery end via a flamethrower, leaving Detective Winston tasked with questioning the two unlikely suspects, Sophia and Virgil.

As Winston closed the victim's office door behind him, he hummed a tune from one of the old tunes he had heard growing up. A home office painted with scorch marks and scars from flames, not the ordinary scene he would walk into. Mackenzie's death was indeed beyond ordinary.

A local artist, Sophia, was on Winston's list for interviews. The name Sophia resonated in the art world, known for her bizarre fire-based creations. Winston remembered; the art reviews had used words like "charred" to describe her artwork. Moreover, he knew that she was often seen transporting flamethrowers to her studio, intriguing the townsfolk. It was said that she used these flamethrowers in her creative process.

Winston found Sophia in her studio, surrounded by antiques that greatly resemble family heirlooms. "Yes, that's me," Sophia replied, pushing her disheveled hair behind her ear. Her face was thin and pale. Dark circles hung heavy under her eyes.

"You purchase a lot of antiques, Sophia?" Winston had noticed the receipt and the dealer's confirmation of the high prices.

"Yes, I do," Sophia replied, casting a glance around her at the collected objects. "They're all pretty expensive, but worth the uniqueness they bring to my art."

Winston decided to press about a more sensitive issue. "Mackenzie," he said, and Sophia's expression shifted. "She found your stash, didn't she?"

Sophia’s face paled even further. "No comment," she muttered, but her jittery hands gave her away.

"I understand she had been funding your art and supporting your addiction habit...your addiction, Sophia," Winston added the words slipping past his lips. He revealed how Mackenzie had threatened to cut Sophia off from her art funds unless she got clean and to tell the world about Sophia's addiction if she didn't get help.

Sophia looked away, a flame dancing in her eyes, mirroring the charred elements in her artwork. In those eyes, Winston found a desperate artist drowning in her own addiction and, the financial torment that was coming along with it. A need for money, for drugs.

"Sophia, her threats...you did hear them, didn't you?" Winston's voice was low.

Sophia, barely audible, whispered, "I heard her."

The evidence was there: the futile search for family heirlooms, the expensive antiques, the thinly-veiled threats from Mackenzie, all leading towards an artist struggling with her addiction. An artist desperate for money and lost in her need for drugs.

"Thank you, Sophia," Winston stood from his chair, but before he left, his eyes trained on a flamethrower stored in the corner of the studio. With these parting words, he left, "Take care of yourself, Sophia."

As Detective Winston entered Virgil's home gym, the smell of iron and sweat filled his nostrils. Walls lined with mirrors reflected the image of a man who spent a great deal of time building his formidable strength and size through lifting heavy weights. 

"Detective," Virgil called out in a deep, gravelly voice, his muscular arms moving a stacked barbell with almost mechanical precision. "Couldn't help but notice Mackenzie in your stack of files."

"She mentioned you helped her out around her home office. Moving heavy things and such?" Winston questioned, observing Virgil's intense workout regime. 

"Helped her plenty, Detective. Many times, she'd call needing my strength." He said, pausing to wipe away the sweat that trickled down his forehead. 

"According to witnesses, your last visit to Mackenzie's wasn't so friendly," Winston remarked, his gaze intense, "You were spotted over at Mackenzie's house on the day she was murdered."

Virgil set down the weight he had been lifting and turned to face Winston. "Yes, the witnesses are correct. I was at her house that day, but I swear I didn't kill her." He admitted.

Detective Winston noticed a glass cabinet filled with an assortment of exotic weaponry. Virgil seemed to be someone who appreciated the unusual; the flamethrower that sat amidst the collection was proof of that. Winston's eyes narrowed slightly at the sight of it. 

"A flamethrower," He pointed out. "Not something you see every day."

Virgil nodded, his arms crossed over his chest. "I do have a penchant for the extraordinary." 

Winston noticed a glaring void on the trophy shelf, amidst the other varied bodybuilding accolites Virgil had accrued. Virgil followed his gaze.

"That's where my prized trophy used to sit. Winning it took an awful lot out of me...quite literally." Virgil's voice betrayed a hint of vulnerability. 

"A piece of metal making you this emotional?" Winston asked, looking at the bodybuilder, his brows lifted in feigned curiosity. 

"Means a lot more to me than just that, Detective," Virgil was quick to retort, his eyes brimming with a mix of anger and sadness, "Especially after you work hard, and the fruits of that labor are just taken away...stolen and sold off like some trinket."

"Mackenzie did that?" Winston inquired, recalling from the witnesses' statements about her selling Virgil's trophy.

"Sure did, Detective. Laughed in my face about it too. Mocked me for placing such value on it." Virgil’s voice tightened around the final words, raw feelings evident in his gaze.

Winston took a deep breath, processing all the information. "I appreciate your honesty, Virgil. I will be on my way now."

With that, Detective Winston left the brawny bodybuilder standing amidst the mirrored room.

In the aftermath of a devastating home explosion that claims the life of Angela, seasoned Detective Winston hones in on two prime suspects: Patrick and Alvin.

Detective Winston winced a little as he pulled up to Angela's home. What was once a well kept, welcoming residence was now charred remains. All due to an explosion powerful enough to shake the neighborhood. As he began his investigation into the events leading up to the incident, one name kept surfacing: Patrick, local surfing instructor and part-time demolition worker who frequently had to handle, use, and was often training on disposing explosives at his job as a requirement of safety measures.
 
To understand this suspect more, Winston set off to meet the man at his next surfing lesson. Under the blistering sun, Patrick was there, quick to anger, bellowing at his students who seemed more frightened than focused on the waves. Several students have had grievances about his harsh teaching methods, which translated to Winston as a lack of patience.

When the session started, Winston noticed the scar that ran down the side of his face which looked ill-treated. Patrick noticed him too. His tall and sturdy figure smirked and sauntered towards Winston. "Detective, right?" his voice was rough, like sandpaper against a rough surface. "Heard about Angela, disturbing really." 

Patrick's nonchalance bothered Winston, but he gave an understanding nod. "Yeah, it is. You were doing demolition work part-time, handling and using explosives, and even have been frequently training on disposing of them, right? That could surely be a dangerous work, isn't it?" Winston queried.

"Sure is," Patrick answered, side-glancing towards his students who were still trying to catch a wave, "Just like surfing, you know, it's all about control." 

Later, Winston found out from the old records that Patrick once worked in a prison. An inmate had assaulted him, and despite being injured, he'd managed to subdue the prisoner. The incident had left him off fieldwork due to minor injuries, but his bravery had been noted. 

Winston also learned that Patrick borrowed a large sum of money from Angela. A neighbor heard Angela frequently threatening to call the cops on Patrick, but he was always around. Patrick had been seen near Angela's home that evening, the very scene of the explosion. There were no others found in the vicinity at the time.

Now, it seemed Winston was dealing with a surfing instructor who vented his frustrations on his students, an injured prison-personnel-turned-demolition-worker with frequent training on handling and disposing explosives who borrowed heavily from a woman who is now dead and was glimpsed around her house before the explosion. Interesting, certainly, but Winston knew there was more to uncover before any real pieces could begin to fall into place here. This was just the start.

Winston sat in his car, surveying through the battered fence that surrounded Angela's suburban home. The yellow tape marking off the scene of the crime fluttered eerily in the wind. Within that marked perimeter was devastation... an explosion had taken place there recently.

As Winston stepped out of his vehicle, a mail truck adorned with cheerful, vibrant colors pulled up to a house down the street. It was Alvin, a well-liked figure in the community, known best for his calm demeanor and reliability. Ex-military, he was now a delivery man and today, just like every day, he was doing his rounds. Along with the rumors of Alvin's unusual fascination with Angela and his tendency to lurk outside her home during unexpected hours, several witnesses had observed Alvin frequently retreating to his garage, where he kept a collection of various artifacts, including explosives and old photos of Angela.

Alvin had scheduled stops all over the neighborhood, but Angela - the victim in Winston's case - was one that he had on his list daily. It was on Alvin's delivery sheet that day too - a package was scheduled for Angela's house. Always punctual, Alvin would hand-deliver packages to Angela; she was always home to receive them, waiting for him at her front door with a box of his old photos of her flashed to Alvin’s mind. 

Angela's old housekeeper clued Winston in on something else. She sat, frail and teary-eyed, as she told him that Angela had recently filed a restraining order against Alvin. Despite this, he continued to visit her home with deliveries daily, revealing a persistence that bordered on stalking. 

"I learned about a lot of things in the army, Winston. How to survive on tinned beans, how to make a fire, how to assemble a rifle... Yes, I might have learnt a bit about explosives too, and have some at my place, but they're never intended for any harm," Alvin responds, visibly tense.

Winston catches sight of the mail truck and the single, small box addressed to Angela seated in the front. It was clear the last delivery of the day was made to her and it was also known that Angela was there to receive it. Angela's neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, a nosy old lady who saw everything on the block had testified to Angela personally receiving the parcel at around the same time the explosion incident occurred.

Long after Winston had left, Alvin continued to stare at the spot where Winston had been sitting, his calm exterior shattered. With dread, he remembered the package marked "explosive" in his garage, along with a stack of Angela's old photos, and the parcel he had delivered just days before Angela's house had gone up in flames.

Target case file:

In the impeccably polished kitchen where Tessa met her fatal end through a deadly gas, Detective Winston starts his journey of dark secrets, questioning Penelope and Melody, the two prime suspects.

Winston pored over the evidence in Tessa's kitchen. The clues were frustratingly scarce - no fingerprints, no forced entry, and the murder weapon, poisonous gas, a lethal specter leaving no traceable footprints. He put on a pair of gloves and sifted through the crime scene photos, his eyes resting on one of Penelope, Tessa's tarot card reader.

Penelope, decked in an extravagant costume, stood out against the throng of guests at the gala. The disguise concealed much of her face, but it was an ineffective veil for her true intent. Winston wasn't looking for her in person; he was instead hoping to unravel the layers of her past.

He turned his attention to the stream of reports from the other officer. No one remembered conversing with Penelope throughout the evening. Winston rubbed his stubbled chin.

"Got a statement saying Penelope was alone in Tessa's kitchen during her tarot reading session," the officer informed Winston. "And she was seen arriving prior to the murder. And just before the time of the murder, multiple witnesses claim they saw Penelope hurriedly leaving Tessa's kitchen, disappearing from the view. However, no one reported seeing Penelope leave Tessa's place before Tessa's lifeless body was found".

Winston felt a chill in his spine as he imagined the confrontation that could have happened in the intimacy of Tessa's kitchen. The letters, the crucial evidence in Tessa's hands, holding the ink stains of Penelope's past crimes, would likely have hit Penelope like a freight train. And, according to Winston's informants, Tessa had indeed confronted Penelope about these crimes, engendering a strong reaction in Penelope; her fear was palpable, even to those who had reported the confrontation.

"Well now, Penelope. What have you been up to?" Winston murmured to himself as he placed the stack of documents on his desk.

There was something about Tessa's knowledge about Penelope's past, about Tessa's confrontation, about Penelope's fearful reaction. Plenty of smoke, Winston thought, but where's the fire?

Everything linked together so subtly. He sighed, running his hands through his hair. Despite the baffling circumstances of the case, Winston knew one fact: he had a pressing investigation ahead of him. It was going to be a long night.

Winston sat hunched over a map pinned to a wall, hand gripping a steaming cup of coffee. Spread out on a desk below, a sprawl of case files surrounded an opened notebook filled with scrawls and coffee rings. As a former officer himself, he knew that standard police training involved the handling of dangerous substances. The ring of a phone broke his contemplation and as he picked it up, the familiar voice of the dispatcher told him he was needed at the scene of a potential gas leak. The location sounded familiar. He sighed, downed the last of his coffee, and grabbed his coat.

Arriving at the house, he was surprised to see Officer Melody securing the scene. She was a friendly face, someone he'd dealt with on many occasions. Her patrol fell largely within the residential district, and Tessa's home was one of the many stops on her beat.

The moment he stepped out of his car, the pungent smell of gas filled his nostrils. He quickly made his way to Melody. "Gas leak, huh?" Winston asked, looking at the small, attractive home. Melody turned to him, nodding slowly, "Came in as that, yes," she replied, her voice betraying a hint of concern. "It's Tessa's place..."

Melody led him to the kitchen, where the gas leak had occurred. The cold, lifeless body of Tessa lay sprawled on the floor. As part of her duties, Melody filled out the police report, marking down vital details.

During their conversation, Winston found out that Melody had been on active duty on the day of the murder, her name clearly listed on the roster. It wasn't unexpected. Melody put in more hours than most other officers, often going above and beyond her duties.

As Melody was talking, Winston's gaze was drawn to a certificate hung on the wall of her patrol car denoting her authorized clearance to use poisonous gas in the case of an emergency. The police department did keep a small supply for situations that demanded it, and Melody, like all other officers, had been trained in the handling of such dangerous substances.

Winston learned a shocking fact as he delved into the case. Tessa's bakery, which sat right in the middle of Melody's patrol zone, was the only establishment that was hindering the territorial expansion Melody had been working towards. The bakery had been a bone of contention for Melody, who had made several offers to Tessa trying to negotiate some form of compromise. But Tessa, it seems, had flatly refused every single one.

As Winston departed the crime scene, he noted that Melody had taken additional courses on handling hazardous materials. But she had always considered herself to be a vigilant public servant. A protector. And as he looked back at Tessa's house, surrounded by yellow tape, he made a note to dig deeper. To understand how the life of a simple baker could intersect so tragically with that of a devoted police officer, and a gas leak that became deadly.

Background files from related investigations (some may be irrelevant):

In the glitz and glamour of a bustling casino, a deadly secret unfolds as Iris is found lifeless by a lead pipe, leaving Detective Winston with two puzzling suspects - Madison and Christine.

Winston struck a match, lighting his pipe and eyeing his case files splayed out on the desk before him. He had a slight headache after a long day of looking into the mysterious death of a lady called Iris. A sad story really, she was a frequent visitor at the casino, she had the luck of a devil. She often walked out of that place with a smile on her face and a hefty amount in her purse...until the night she didn't walk out at all.

Sifting through the evidence, Winston's hand found an envelope labeled 'Confidential.' Inside, there was a recorded statement Iris had given to a trusted friend a few days before her death. Iris clearly expressed her intention to report Christine at her next police visit.

The only real link he had to the case so far was Christine. Christine was a solid, muscular woman who worked long hours at a construction site. It wasn't just her construction job that kept her fit, it was also the time she spent with Iris working on a shared construction project. It was during these long hours they spent together that they built a strong association, a teamwork which often led them to the casino.

Christine, during one of their teamwork endeavors revealed to Iris her involvement in certain illicit activities. Iris, shocked by this revelation, clearly intended to report these activities to the police, a fact she expressed in the recorded statement Winston now held in his hands.

Another peculiar detail, a lead pipe -- the same type as the murder weapon -- was discovered at Christine and Iris's collective work site. Christine certainly had the brawn to wield that pipe.

Winston flipped open the file and spread out the still shots from the casino's surveillance footage. A timestamp in the corner corroborated with his notes -- Christine was present at the casino the night of the murder.

The police station was quiet as he entered Christine's holding cell. The woman looked tense but tried to put up a brave front.

"Spending a lot of time at the casino and the construction site these days?" He asked.

"Sure, ever since Iris and I started working on that project together. We often celebrated our small victories at the casino" Christine's voice choked a bit on her friend's name.

"And during those hours you told Iris about your...extra-curricular activities?" Winston pressed further. Christine didn't deny it, remained silent.

"Iris had planned to turn you in you know?" Winston said coolly, fanning out the recorded statement. "This was her intention during her upcoming visit to the police station."

Christine didn't respond, just locked her gaze onto Winston's.

"I noticed a lead pipe lying around your shared construction site, identical to the murder weapon," he pushed further. "Now, Christine, what else did you two discuss when you were working on those projects?"

Winston sat back, letting his words linger in the chill air of the interview room. The pieces of the puzzle were slowly falling into place, but the game was far from over.

Detective Winston scoured through the casino surveillance footage once again, his grim reflection faintly visible on the monitor screen. There was Madison, peering into what looked like a 'souvenir' box, a curious mix of nostalgia and uncertainty etched on their face. Not a lead, but perhaps another piece of the puzzle.

A separate clip caught Winston's eye, revealing Iris within the casino, merrily wagering lady luck amidst a sea of other gamblers. Iris and Madison under the same roof. It made sense something had transpired, but it was not his place yet to jump to conclusions.

Subsequent investigation took Winston to Madison's apartment. Reports had come in that they were often seen witnessing Iris's Friday night departures for the casino. Madison, it seemed, had an insight into Iris's late-night gambling endeavors, if only because they both shared the same neighborhood.

A new twist arrived in the form of an overheard conversation. Madison, just within earshot of Winston's position, seemed to be reminiscing about overhearing Iris's tales of the casino's allure. It didn't boost the investigation, but it added an interesting dynamic.

As the day wore on, Winston moved to the next building with a lead. Madison, seen using a key to enter the previous tenant's apartment, raised some questions. On being questioned about possessing this particular key, Madison nostalgically said, "Ah, such memories." The janitor confirmed that Madison had indeed requested a copy of the previous occupant's keys. A favor for an old friend or something more sinister?

The detective moved his inquiry to the legal hullabaloo that suddenly had Iris at the heart of it. Surveillance footage showed her in the courthouse with an armful of court documents. Iris was no ordinary casino patron but a key witness in a court case directly linked to Madison's illegal activities. This implied a new layer of complication to their association.

Legal terms printed on an eviction notice in Madison's possession stated that any illegal activities could lead to immediate eviction. Madison, having received this, was acutely aware of the implications of Iris' testimony.  A visit to the casino and the courthouse, another twist in the tale, was when Madison's lawyer had to break the news to their client about Iris's damning testimony.

But for Winston, there was still a bunch of questions left unanswered, and the jigsaw was only half complete. The investigation had to dig deeper. There was a long day ahead. Pieces were moving, and Winston knew well enough in this game; nothing moved without a reason.

In the hushed silence of the library, Floyd lay dead with a shiv protruding from his chest, prompting Detective Winston to weave through the labyrinth of books and suspicion, targeting his primary suspects, Zara and Catherine.

After the news of Floyd's death, Winston found himself surrounded by books, cameras, and whispers. Libraries were supposed to bring tranquility, but now, this one seemed to echo with the whispers of a crime. The forensic team had found punctured wounds on Floyd's body, a mixture of peculiar cuts and punches, that were oddly similar to those that could be inflicted with a shiv; the kind that could easily be improvised with sharp tools. This had resulted in his untimely demise.

He had just visited Floyd's library, shifting through the catalogue of CCTV feed. It showed Zara entering the library during the day. She had a fairly regular routine, according to the library personnel. Winston also caught a glimpse of her re-emerging later, her steps were quick and purposeful. 

Winston kept his thoughts grounded, going through the notes he made during his interrogation session. Who was Zara, besides the latest burning face of the fashion industry? Her social media was a cascade of her embracing scissors, needles and other sharp filaments in her ostensible designs. Objects that, considering enough technique, can be reshaped into a dangerous weapon like a shiv.

He flipped through the photos of Zara's workspace. There was a toolkit - an array of sharp, glimmering instruments specifically designed for crafting fashion. They also gave Winston a hint of a chilling familiarity with the puncture evidence.

Later, Winston found himself in front of a small, quaint house. From here he could clearly see it, the neighbor's living room window faced directly onto Zara's driveway. The neighbor, a night owl of sorts, spent most of his time binge-watching on Netflix. He had always been proud of his knack for precision-perfect timing.

He had another reliable source too - Zara's older brother. Often, due to an insomniac streak, he would visit Zara at night to check up on her. Each time, he noticed the room light would go off, followed soon by the faint hum of her car starting. 

"Tell me again," Winston asked both of them in turn, "when did you hear Zara's car start?"

"Just after her room light went off," they iterated, almost in chorus, "like clockwork."

Evidently, Floyd the book lover's final day, a day spent around books, had an unexpected visitor - Zara. The pieces fell away like breadcrumbs leading into an obscure path. Winston knew this monumental work could unravel itself only with time. For now, it was time for the detective to take a coffee break, before immersing into the enigma once again.

After a long day of gathering information and different pieces of evidence, Winston found himself heading towards the residence of a pilot named Catherine. Floyd, the victim, was found dead in the library with obvious signs he was attacked with a sharp object, possibly a shiv. Detailed research unclosed particulars about Catherine's time in the military where she learned to use a unique blade like a shiv. Catherine admitted that after her military days, she continued to feel safer practicing using her shiv which she always carried with her.  This significant piece of information is what led Winston here, to question Catherine directly. 

"Good evening, Catherine," Winston began upon her opening the door, "I trust you were expecting me?" Catherine's slightly widened eyes suggested otherwise, but she still opened the door further, welcoming him inside. 

"I am sorry for the inconvenience, but I need to ask a few questions regarding Floyd."

"Floyd?" She asked. "What has happened?"

Winston said, "Our investigation revealed that he was continuously asking you for the money you owed him." He further added, “He was planning to take legal action if you didn’t pay, proof of which we found in his office."

Upon hearing this, Catherine responded, "Yes, he was putting me under a lot of pressure to pay back.” She then pointed towards her busy calendar placed on her desk and revealed, "We had a meeting scheduled today at the library to discuss the matter, it's right there in the calendar."

Confirming Floyd's attendance at the meeting Winston adds, "Yes, we've checked the library's sign-in book and confirmed that Floyd did check in for the meeting."

Catherine shrugged. "I was supposed to meet him there. About my debts to him."

"Your debts..?" Winston asked, raising an eyebrow. "Would you care to talk more about it?"

"Not much to say detective," shrugged Catherine, "I owed him money... wasn't able to pay."

"Why weren't you able to pay this debt?"

She sighed heavily with a far off gaze in her eyes as truth revealed itself. "I'd been missing a lot of mortgage payments. Had to sell my airplane. Just haven't been able to make ends meet..."

Winston shifted his gaze to a bag that sat on a nearby desk. Marked beside it were a few library books. Catherine followed Winston's gaze. "I took them from the library," she admitted. That would explain why her fingerprints were all over the books.

Winston smirked lightly. "And the librarian confirmed seeing you there, around the time of Floyd’s murder.”

With an unsettling chuckle, he switched the topic "I heard you were in the military?"

Catherine nodded. "Yes, I was."

"The military - where we learn a lot, including how to use a shiv I am assuming?”

Catherine chuckled lightly. "Well, yes. And as you can see," she pointed towards her bag on her desk, wherein upon casual inspection Winston found the shiv, "I never stopped practicing. It makes me feel safe to have it with me."

The shiv perfectly fit the description of the blade used in the murder of Floyd. It was the perfect weapon for a practiced hand to use quickly and quietly in a crowded library. 

But Winston merely nodded to himself as he jotted down a note or two. "You're full of surprises, Catherine."

They spent a couple more minutes talking aimlessly about life, the military, and Catherine's days in the air. But finally, Winston stood, getting ready to leave.

"I'll be back if I have more questions. Good evening Catherine."

As Winston drove away, his mind replayed back the facts he had collected throughout the day; Catherine's debts, her financial struggles, Floyd's continuous pressure for the money Catherine owed, Floyd's plan to take legal action, their planned meeting at the library, her continued practice with the blade, the missed mortgage payments, Catherine’s military background, the identified shiv in her bag, her bold admission of always feeling safer with her shiv and possibly most incriminating, the librarian’s testimony...

His job was merely about gathering the facts. The rest was for the law and the jury to decide.
